source.title: On the Beilinson fiber square
source.authors: Benjamin Antieau, Akhil Mathew, Matthew Morrow, Thomas Nikolaus
source.read: arXiv v2 (29 September 2021), the last preprint version, whose comment records many minor updates from the referee reports and a new, simplified proof of the integral comparison theorem for syntomic cohomology; it postdates the referee process and precedes publication in December 2022. Read in the LaTeX source of that version (arXiv e-print of 2003.12541v2, file Beilinson-revised-arXivstyle.tex, 5577 lines, sha256 of the source archive 289e0749087870768d471ca7dda1146dd896cdb0f88cef1e07215c08789462c0), fetched 22 September 2026. Duke Mathematical Journal is not open access and the published text could not be consulted here, so every locator below is a preprint number and the two source issues are recorded against the preprint, with no claim about the published version. The preprint numbers all environments by a single counter per section, Definition 2.1, Remark 2.2, Example 2.3 and so on, which is the numbering used throughout; the two appendices are numbered A.n and B.n. Statements labelled by letters in the introduction — Theorems A, C, D, E, F, G and Corollaries B, H — are unnumbered and are recorded at their numbered counterparts in the body: A at Theorem 2.12 with Corollary 3.9, B at Theorem 2.20, C at Theorem 3.4, D at Theorem 4.9, E at Theorem 4.14, F at Theorem 6.22, G at Theorem 5.1 and H at Corollary 6.23.
readSections: Independent review: all 65 pages of arXiv:2003.12541v2, including all proofs, Appendices A/B and references.
Published 100-page reprint: compared only the source-finding and corrected-statement passages, not a complete second reading.
Supporting primary passages: Bhatt12 pp32–33; SZ18 pp32–36; BEK14 author final PDF pp1–3. Other cited external proofs remain open boundaries.

summary: The paper constructs the Beilinson K/TC/cyclic-homology square and its integral quasi-isogeny refinements, proves p-adic K-class deformation and syntomic/Fontaine–Messing comparisons, and derives local-field and period-ring consequences. This independently corrected extraction is partial: generic foundations are imported, three exact library items are reused, and transitive proof/API and arbitrary-perfectoid comparison gaps remain explicit.

items.name: Goodwillie's theorem
items.statement: If I ⊆ R is a nilpotent ideal in an associative Q-algebra R, then the square with rows K(R) → K(R/I) and HC^-(R) → HC^-(R/I) and vertical Goodwillie–Jones trace maps is cartesian; equivalently tr_GJ : K(R, I) → HC^-(R, I) is an equivalence on relative theories.
items.note: RT.3 plans the rational relative K-theory/cyclic-homology comparison with its stated nilpotence hypotheses, and names the excision, approximation and convergence inputs of the chosen proof as subtargets.

items.name: The Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy theorem
items.statement: If I ⊆ R is a nilpotent ideal in an associative ring R, then the square with rows K(R) → K(R/I) and TC(R) → TC(R/I) and vertical cyclotomic trace maps is cartesian; equivalently tr : K(R, I) → TC(R, I) is an equivalence on relative theories.
items.note: RT.3 plans the relative nilpotent comparison theorem with its connective input and p-completion assumptions; this is its integral form and the engine of everything K-theoretic in this paper.

items.name: The p-adic variational Hodge conjecture (Fontaine–Messing)
items.statement: Define the Fontaine–Messing p-adic variational Hodge conjecture as the following proposition, with no proof asserted: Let O_K be a complete DVR of mixed characteristic with perfect residue field k, X a proper smooth O_K-scheme with special fibre X_k and generic fibre X_K, and α ∈ H^even_dR(X_K/K). Then α is in the image of the Chern character from K_0(X; Q) if and only if (1) the image of α under the de Rham-to-crystalline isomorphism in H^even_crys(X_k) ⊗_{W(k)} K lies in the image of the crystalline Chern character from K_0(X_k; Q), and (2) α lies in ⊕_i Fil^{≥i} H^{2i}_dR(X_K/K).
items.note: The conjecture the paper's Section 4 works towards; it is not proved here. MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.7 plans typed statements of the Hodge, Tate and standard conjectures and a register of proved cases, but the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture is not among them, and neither is the continuous K-theory in which it is formulated.

items.name: Cyclotomic spectra, TC^-, TP and TC
items.statement: CycSp denotes the symmetric monoidal stable ∞-category of (p-typical) cyclotomic spectra: a spectrum X with an S^1-action and an S^1-equivariant cyclotomic Frobenius φ_p : X → X^{tC_p}. For X ∈ CycSp one sets TC^-(X) = X^{hS^1} and TP(X) = X^{tS^1}, with two maps can, φ : TC^-(X; Z_p) → TP(X; Z_p), the first the canonical map from homotopy fixed points to the Tate construction and the second induced by φ_p. For X bounded below, p-complete topological cyclic homology is TC(X; Z_p) = fib(can − φ : TC^-(X; Z_p) → TP(X; Z_p)).
items.note: RT.2 constructs cyclotomic spectra by the Nikolaus–Scholze Frobenius maps to Tate fixed points, with the residual circle action and prime indexing, and constructs TC, TC^- and TP with their comparison maps and the bounded-below hypotheses under which the fixed-point formula applies.

items.name: Basic cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: (1) For a ring R, THH(R) is a cyclotomic spectrum. (2) For a spectrum Y, Y^triv is the cyclotomic spectrum with trivial S^1-action and cyclotomic Frobenius the natural map Y → Y^{hC_p} → Y^{tC_p}. (3) For a spectrum X with S^1-action, taking φ_p : X → X^{tC_p} to be zero as an S^1-equivariant map gives a cyclotomic spectrum.
items.note: The trivial and zero-Frobenius cyclotomic structures are part of RT.2's construction of the category; they are used throughout this paper to compare TC with cyclic homology.

items.name: Tensoring TC with a trivial cyclotomic spectrum
items.statement: Let Y be a bounded below spectrum of finite type. If X ∈ CycSp is p-complete and bounded below, then there is a natural equivalence TC(X ⊗_S Y^triv; Z_p) ≃ TC(X; Z_p) ⊗_S Y. This holds for Y merely bounded below provided the right-hand side is p-completed.
items.note: A consequence of the fact that TC(−; Z_p) commutes with geometric realizations of connective cyclotomic spectra and carries n-connective objects to (n−1)-connective ones. RT.2 constructs TC but does not plan this tensor formula, which the paper uses to split off the trivial part of the square.

items.name: TC when TP vanishes
items.statement: If X ∈ CycSp is bounded below and TP(X; Z_p) = 0, then there are natural equivalences TC(X; Z_p) ≃ (Σ X_{hS^1})^∧_p ≃ TC^-(X; Z_p).
items.note: The mechanism that converts the cyclotomic input into cyclic homology; it is what makes the fibre of the Beilinson square a suspension of HC.

items.name: The cyclotomic spectrum Z_{hC_p}
items.statement: The cyclotomic trace gives a map Z^triv → THH(F_p) in CycSp, and in Fun(BS^1, Sp) one has THH(F_p) ≃ τ_{≥0}(Z^{tC_p}), the S^1-action on Z^{tC_p} coming from C_p → S^1 →^{z↦z^p} S^1; this refines Bökstedt's calculation of THH(F_p). Hence there is a cofibre sequence Z_{hC_p} → Z^triv → THH(F_p) in CycSp whose first term has underlying S^1-spectrum Z_{hC_p}. One has (Z_{hC_p})^{tC_p} ≃ 0 by the Tate orbit lemma, so Z^triv → THH(F_p) induces an equivalence on TP(−; Z_p), i.e. Z_p^{tS^1} ≃ TP(F_p), and TC(Z_{hC_p}; Z_p) ≃ Σ(Z_p)_{hS^1}.
items.note: The central construction of Section 2: the cyclotomic spectrum whose TC is the suspension of the cyclic-homology term. Nothing in the atlas plans it; RT.2 plans THH(F_p) and the Tate orbit lemma in the Nikolaus–Scholze range that this is built from.

items.name: Tate vanishing for Z_{hC_p}
items.statement: If X ∈ Fun(BS^1, Sp), then (X ⊗_S Z_{hC_p})^{tS^1} is p-adically zero, where S^1 acts diagonally.
items.note: The vanishing that makes the square of the next item cartesian.

items.name: The basic cartesian square of cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: Let X ∈ CycSp be bounded below. Then the square with rows TC(X ⊗_S Z^triv; Z_p) → TC(X ⊗_S THH(F_p); Z_p) and TC^-(X ⊗_S Z^triv; Z_p) → TC^-(X ⊗_S THH(F_p); Z_p), horizontal maps induced by Z^triv → THH(F_p) and vertical maps the canonical TC → TC^-, is cartesian. Moreover there is a natural fibre sequence (Σ(X ⊗_S Z_{hC_p})_{hS^1})^∧_p → TC(X ⊗_S Z^triv; Z_p) → TC(X ⊗_S THH(F_p); Z_p).
items.note: The cyclotomic form of the Beilinson square, before specialising to rings.

items.name: The fibre sequence for a connective ring spectrum
items.statement: For every connective ring spectrum R there is a natural fibre sequence of p-complete spectra Σ(THH(R; Z_p) ⊗_S Z_{hC_p})_{hS^1} → TC(R; Z_p) ⊗_S Z → TC(R ⊗_S F_p; Z_p).
items.note: The ring-level specialisation of the previous item.

items.name: The square with TC^- and TP
items.statement: Let X ∈ CycSp be bounded below and p-complete. Then there is a natural map TC(X ⊗_S THH(F_p); Z_p) → (X ⊗_S Z^triv)^{tS^1} fitting into a natural commutative square with rows TC(X ⊗_S Z^triv; Z_p) → TC(X ⊗_S THH(F_p); Z_p) and (X ⊗_S Z^triv)^{hS^1} → (X ⊗_S Z^triv)^{tS^1}, and this square becomes cartesian after inverting p.
items.note: The step at which p has to be inverted; the total cofibre is torsion but not zero.

items.name: Effective bounds on the denominators
items.statement: The total cofibre of the square of the previous item is Σ^2(X ⊗_S THH(F_p))_{hS^1}. If X is connective, then τ_{≤2i} of the total cofibre is annihilated by p^i, because τ_{≤2i−2}THH(F_p) is S^1-equivariantly annihilated by p^i: its homotopy is concentrated in even degrees and each group is an F_p-vector space, so the S^1-equivariant Postnikov filtration has i stages.
items.note: The quantitative form of the previous item; it is what makes the integral statements of Section 2 and the range 2p−5 of Corollary B possible.

items.name: The Beilinson fibre square
items.statement: Let R be a ring, or more generally a connective associative HZ-algebra spectrum. Then there is a natural commutative square of spectra with rows TC(R; Z_p) → TC(R ⊗_S F_p) and HC^-(R; Z_p) → HP(R; Z_p), which becomes cartesian after inverting p. Apart from the right vertical arrow, all maps are the canonical ones.
items.note: RT.3b plans exactly this theorem, together with Corollary 3.9, insisting that Q_p mean p-completion followed by inversion of p and that the spectral reduction R ⊗_S F_p be distinguished from the ordinary ring R/p.

items.name: Effective bounds for the Beilinson square
items.statement: For i ≤ p−1, τ_{≤2i} of the total cofibre of the Beilinson square is annihilated by p^i. The map on cofibres of the bottom rows of the two squares is Σ^2(THH(R) ⊗_S Z^triv)_{hS^1} → Σ^2 HH(R; Z_p)_{hS^1}, which is an equivalence in degrees ≤ 2p−2.
items.note: The effective bound for the ring-level square; it is the source of every range of the form 2p − c in the paper.

items.name: The p-adic Chern character
items.statement: Let R be a ring. After inverting p one has TC(R ⊗_S F_p; Q_p) ≃ TC(R/p; Q_p), giving a map β : TC(R/p; Q_p) → HP(R; Q_p); precomposing with the cyclotomic trace gives the p-adic Chern character tr_crys = β ∘ tr : K(R/p; Q_p) → HP(R; Q_p). It fits into a natural diagram with rows K(R; Q_p) → K(R/p; Q_p), TC(R; Q_p) → TC(R/p; Q_p) and HC^-(R; Q_p) → HP(R; Q_p), in which the bottom square is a pullback.
items.note: RT.3b plans the construction of both vertical maps of the square, of which this is the right-hand one together with its factorisation through the trace; it is the map called tr_crys in Theorem A.

items.name: Clausen–Mathew–Morrow's theorem
items.statement: If R is commutative and henselian along (p), then the cyclotomic trace induces an equivalence K(R, (p); Z_p) ≃ TC(R, (p); Z_p).
items.note: RT.3 plans the relative comparison for a henselian pair in the proven range and exports the map-level square; it is the input that turns every TC statement of this paper into a K-theory statement.

items.name: The associative p-complete case
items.statement: If R is associative, p-complete and has bounded p-power torsion, then there is an equivalence lim_n K(R/p^n, (p)) ≃ TC(R, (p); Z_p), by the Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy theorem and the p-adic continuity of TC.
items.note: The substitute for Clausen–Mathew–Morrow's theorem when R is not commutative; it is what lets the K-theoretic corollaries be stated for continuous K-theory of associative rings.

items.name: Isogenies and quasi-isogenies
items.statement: In an additive (∞-)category C a map f : X → Y is an isogeny if there are g : Y → X and an integer N > 0 with g ∘ f = N·id_X and f ∘ g = N·id_Y. If C is stable with a left-complete t-structure, a map f : X → Y of bounded below objects is a quasi-isogeny if, equivalently, (1) τ_{≤n}f is an isogeny in C for every n, or (2) π_n X → π_n Y is an isogeny in the heart for every n.
items.note: Shared categorical notion at E2/E5:abstract, used by RT.3b. Degreewise denominators need not admit one bound valid in every degree; a natural transformation has bounds uniform in its indexing objects.

planningApi.name: isogeny
planningApi.signature: For an additive category C and f:X→Y, witnesses are N∈Z_{>0} and g:Y→X with gf=N·id_X and fg=N·id_Y.

planningApi.name: quasiIsogeny
planningApi.signature: In a stable category with left-complete t-structure and bounded-below X,Y, require each truncation τ≤n(f) to be an isogeny; prove equivalence to the heartwise condition.

planningApi.name: naturalQuasiIsogeny
planningApi.signature: Apply the definition in Fun(I,C) with pointwise t-structure, keeping each denominator independent of i∈I.

unitTests.statement: Multiplication by a nonzero integer on HZ is an isogeny.
The coproduct of H(Z/p^r), r≥1, in degree zero is torsion but not killed by one integer: its map to zero is not an isogeny.
Changing degreewise bounds must not silently give one bound in all degrees.

items.name: Theorem A and Corollary B: TC(R,(p)) is quasi-isogenous to ΣHC
items.statement: For any associative ring R the spectra TC(R, (p); Z_p), ΣHC(R, (p); Z_p) and ΣHC(R; Z_p) are naturally quasi-isogenous to each other. Moreover (a) if R is p-torsion free the first two are equivalent after (2p−5)-truncation, and (b) if in addition π_{−1}(TC(R; Z_p)) = 0 they are equivalent after (2p−4)-truncation. Combined with Clausen–Mathew–Morrow's theorem this gives, for R commutative and henselian along (p), a natural zig-zag of quasi-isogenies between K(R, (p); Z_p) and ΣHC(R, (p); Z_p), with π_i K(R,(p);Z_p) ≅ π_i ΣHC(R,(p);Z_p) for i ≤ 2p−5 when R is p-torsion free.
items.note: The integral refinement of Theorem A, stated as Corollary B in the introduction. RT.3b plans the rational square and the rational identification of its fibre with ΣHC; the integral quasi-isogeny and the explicit truncation ranges are not planned there and are what Section 7's integral K-theory calculations rest on.

items.name: Integral HZ linearization of TC is a quasi-isogeny
items.statement: The map TC(R; Z_p) → TC(R; Z_p) ⊗_S Z is a natural quasi-isogeny of spectra, and its fibre is (2p−4)-connective; if π_{−1}(TC(R; Z_p)) = 0 the fibre is (2p−3)-connective.
items.note: One of the three quasi-isogenies assembled into the previous theorem.

items.name: The spectral and ordinary reductions mod p agree up to isogeny
items.statement: The natural map TC(R ⊗_S F_p; Z_p) → TC(R/p; Z_p) is a quasi-isogeny; if R is p-torsion free its fibre is (2p−1)-connective.
items.note: This is what makes the Beilinson square a statement about the ordinary ring R/p rather than about the spectral reduction; RT.3b names the distinction explicitly and requires this comparison.

items.name: The cyclic-homology term up to quasi-isogeny
items.statement: The spectra (THH(R; Z_p) ⊗_S Z_{hC_p})_{hS^1}, HC(R, (p); Z_p) and HC(R; Z_p) are naturally quasi-isogenous to each other, and the first two are equivalent after (2p−4)-truncation if R is p-torsion free.
items.note: The identification of the fibre term with ordinary cyclic homology.

items.name: The fibre of TC(R) → TC(R ⊗_Z F_p)
items.statement: If R is a connective Z-algebra spectrum, then the fibre of TC(R; Z_p) → TC(R ⊗_Z F_p; Z_p) is quasi-isogenous to ΣHC(R; Z_p), and after (2p−5)-truncation is equivalent to the fibre of ΣHC(R; Z_p) → ΣHC(R ⊗_Z F_p; Z_p).
items.note: The relative form used for nilpotent extensions.

items.name: Relative K-theory of a nilpotent ideal up to quasi-isogeny
items.statement: Let (R, I) be an associative ring with a nilpotent ideal. Then there is a natural zig-zag of quasi-isogenies between K(R, I; Z_p) and ΣHC(R, I; Z_p).
items.note: The p-adic analogue of Goodwillie's theorem: rationally K(R,I) ≃ HC^-(R,I), while p-adically it is ΣHC(R,I) up to bounded denominators. GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.5 plans relative K-theory and RT.3 the rational comparison; this p-adic statement is not planned.

items.name: Detecting quasi-isogenies of cyclotomic spectra by TR
items.statement: A map f : X → Y of bounded-below cyclotomic spectra is a quasi-isogeny in CycSp if and only if TR(f) : TR(X) → TR(Y) is a quasi-isogeny of spectra.
items.note: The criterion by which quasi-isogenies are checked; RT.2 plans the comparison with the classical genuine-equivariant TR/TC formulation, which is the functor used here.

items.name: Nullhomotopic Frobenius and quasi-isogeny to zero
items.statement: Let X ∈ CycSp be bounded below, with cyclotomic Frobenius φ : X → X^{tC_p} nullhomotopic in Fun(BS^1, Sp), and quasi-isogenous to zero as a spectrum. Then X is quasi-isogenous to zero as a cyclotomic spectrum.
items.note: One of the two criteria for a cyclotomic spectrum to vanish up to isogeny.

items.name: Graded criterion for quasi-isogeny to zero
items.statement: Let X be a graded cyclotomic spectrum such that (1) the underlying spectrum is quasi-isogenous to zero, (2) the graded piece X_0 is contractible, and (3) the connectivity of the pieces X_i tends to infinity in i. Then X is quasi-isogenous to zero in CycSp.
items.note: The graded criterion, applied through the twisted Tate diagonal of Appendix A.

items.name: Theorem C: quasi-isogenies of THH
items.statement: Let f : A → A′ be a map of connective associative ring spectra such that (i) f is a quasi-isogeny of spectra and (ii) π_0(f) : π_0(A) → π_0(A′) is surjective with nilpotent kernel. Then THH(A) → THH(A′) is a quasi-isogeny in CycSp; in particular TC(A; Z_p) → TC(A′; Z_p) is a quasi-isogeny.
items.note: Theorem C of the introduction, and the main theorem of Section 3. RT.3b names 'the quasi-isogeny comparison of §3' as the input that distinguishes R ⊗_S F_p from R/p, but does not state this theorem; the paper is its source.

items.name: THH of a graded ring spectrum with small positive part
items.statement: Let R be a connective associative graded ring spectrum such that (a) each R_i for i > 0 is isogenous to zero as a spectrum and (b) the connectivity of the R_i tends to ∞ as i → ∞. Then THH(R) → THH(R_0) is a quasi-isogeny in CycSp.
items.note: The graded case, from which the general case is deduced by a square-zero reduction.

items.name: THH of a square-zero extension by a small bimodule
items.statement: Let A be a connective associative ring spectrum and M a connective (A,A)-bimodule quasi-isogenous to zero. If Ã is the square-zero extension of A by M, i.e. the pullback of A →^{f} A ⊕ M[1] ←^{0} A for a map f : A → A ⊕ M[1] in Alg_{/A}, then THH(Ã) → THH(A) is a quasi-isogeny in CycSp.
items.note: The square-zero case.

items.name: The augmented case
items.statement: Let B be a connective associative ring spectrum and B′ ∈ Alg_{B//B}. If the augmentation B′ → B is a quasi-isogeny and π_0(B′) → π_0(B) has nilpotent kernel, then THH(B) → THH(B′) is a quasi-isogeny.
items.note: The augmented case, from which the general one follows.

items.name: Geisser–Hesselholt: relative K-theory in characteristic p is torsion
items.statement: If p is nilpotent in A and I ⊆ A is a two-sided nilpotent ideal, then K(A, I) ≃ TC(A, I) is quasi-isogenous to zero.
items.note: Recovered here as a corollary of Theorem C; nothing in the atlas plans it. RT.3 plans the relative nilpotent comparison K(A,I) ≃ TC(A,I) itself.

items.name: Corollary 3.9: the Beilinson square for the ordinary reduction
items.statement: Let R be a ring. Then there is a natural pullback square with rows TC(R; Q_p) → TC(R/p; Q_p) and HC^-(R; Q_p) → HP(R; Q_p).
items.note: RT.3b plans exactly this corollary alongside Theorem 2.12, with the instruction to supply the quasi-isogeny comparison of Section 3 that replaces R ⊗_S F_p by R/p.

items.name: THH of a p-adic ring relative to p up to quasi-isogeny
items.statement: For every ring R the cyclotomic spectra THH(R, (p); Z_p), HH(R; Z_p) and HH(R, (p); Z_p) are quasi-isogenous to each other, where the two Hochschild terms carry the canonical S^1-action and the zero Frobenius. If R is p-torsion free there is an equivalence of cyclotomic spectra τ^cyc_{≤2p−4}THH(R, (p); Z_p) ≃ τ^cyc_{≤2p−4}HH(R, (p); Z_p).
items.note: The cyclotomic refinement of the identification of the fibre term with cyclic homology.

items.name: Quasi-isogenies are stable under tensoring
items.statement: If X → Y is a quasi-isogeny of cyclotomic spectra and M is any bounded below cyclotomic spectrum, then X ⊗_S M → Y ⊗_S M is a quasi-isogeny of cyclotomic spectra.
items.note: A permanence property of quasi-isogenies in CycSp.

items.name: The cyclotomic identification of the fibre term
items.statement: The cyclotomic spectra THH(R; Z_p) ⊗_S Z_{hC_p}, HH(R; Z_p) and HH(R, (p); Z_p) are quasi-isogenous to each other, and, if R is p-torsion free, the cyclotomic truncations τ^cyc_{≤2p−4} of the first and third are naturally equivalent.
items.note: The cyclotomic form of the identification used in Section 2.

items.name: Continuous invariants of a p-adic formal scheme
items.statement: Let F be an invariant of schemes (such as K, THH, HH, HC^-, HP or TC) and X a qcqs p-adic formal scheme with bounded p-power torsion with X_n = X ×_{Spec Z} Z/p^n. Define F^cts(X) = lim_n F(X_n). In particular K^cts(X) = lim_n K(X_n) is continuous K-theory.
items.note: The object in which the p-adic deformation problem is posed. GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.5 plans relative K-theory and K.7 filtered-colimit compatibility, but no layer plans the inverse limit over the thickenings of a formal scheme, which is the whole point here.

planningApi.name: continuousInvariant
planningApi.signature: For an invariant F and a qcqs p-adic formal X with bounded p-power torsion, define Fcts(X)=Rlim_n F(X×Z/p^n).

planningApi.name: continuousRestriction
planningApi.signature: The map F(X)→Fcts(X) is induced by restrictions; record naturality in X and compatibility of transition maps.

planningApi.name: rationalContinuousK
planningApi.signature: Set Kcts(X;Q)=Kcts(X)⊗Q only after the inverse limit. Do not exchange rationalization and limit without a theorem.

unitTests.statement: For an affine p-complete ring compare the inverse system with the ring reductions.
For a constant inverse system recover its value.
Keep π0 Rlim and lim π0 distinct until the Milnor lim1 term vanishes.

items.name: Continuity of the trace invariants
items.statement: Suppose X is the p-adic completion of a qcqs scheme X with bounded p-power torsion. Then the comparison maps F(X) → F^cts(X) for F = HH, THH, HC^-, HP, TC are p-adic equivalences. For F = K the same holds when X is affine, i.e. X = Spf(R) for R p-adically complete with bounded p-power torsion.
items.note: The continuity statements that make the continuous invariants computable; for K they rest on Clausen–Mathew–Morrow and Geisser–Hesselholt, and for a proper scheme the K-theoretic statement is expected to fail.

items.name: De Rham cohomology of a smooth formal scheme and its Hodge filtration
items.statement: For a smooth p-adic formal scheme X → Spf(O_K) one has the p-adic de Rham cohomology RΓ_dR(X/O_K) ∈ D(O_K) with its descending multiplicative Hodge filtration Fil^{≥⋆}RΓ_dR(X/O_K); when X is proper these are perfect complexes, and after inverting p one writes RΓ_dR(X_K/K) and Fil^{≥⋆}RΓ_dR(X_K/K). When X is proper, the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence of RΓ_dR(X_K/K) degenerates after rationalization, by Scholze's degeneration theorem for proper smooth rigid analytic varieties.
items.note: DD.2 plans derived de Rham cohomology with its Hodge filtration and DD.1 the p-completion, so the construction itself is available; what is not planned anywhere is the degeneration statement it quotes, Scholze's Hodge-to-de Rham degeneration for proper smooth rigid analytic varieties, which is listed below as a prerequisite. The item is routed with Section 4 because that is where the filtered object is used.

items.name: Comparison between crystalline and de Rham cohomology
items.statement: For a smooth p-adic formal scheme X → Spf(O_K): in the absolutely unramified case O_K = W(k) the de Rham-to-crystalline comparison gives RΓ_crys(X_k) ≃ RΓ_dR(X/O_K); in general, by Berthelot–Ogus, there is a natural equivalence after rationalization RΓ_dR(X_K/K) ≃ RΓ_crys(X_k; Q_p) ⊗_{K_0} K.
items.note: DD.4 constructs the natural map from derived de Rham to crystalline cohomology through PD envelopes and the PD Poincaré lemma, and CP.2 owns the rational crystalline comparison and its descent for a smooth proper formal O_K-model; the Berthelot–Ogus statement is the rationalised comparison they plan.

items.name: The crystalline Chern character
items.statement: Let Y be a regular scheme of characteristic p. For a vector bundle V on Y one defines crystalline Chern classes c_i(V) ∈ H^{2i}_crys(Y) satisfying the usual axioms, and the usual formula yields the crystalline Chern character, a natural ring homomorphism ch_crys : K_0(Y) → ⊕_{i≥0} H^{2i}_crys(Y; Q_p) carrying the class of a line bundle L to exp(c_1(L)) = ∑_{n≥0} c_1(L)^n/n!.
items.note: SchemeKTheoryOperations S.7 constructs Chern classes, the Chern character and the γ-filtration with values in Chow groups, and CR.1/CR.7 construct crystalline crystals and their coefficient interfaces, but the crystalline Chern character itself is planned by neither. It is the invariant in which both the Bloch–Esnault–Kerz theorem and the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture are stated.

items.name: The Bloch–Esnault–Kerz theorem
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero with ring of integers O_K and perfect residue field k of characteristic p > 0, and let X → Spf(O_K) be a proper smooth p-adic formal scheme with special fibre X_k. A class x ∈ K_0(X_k; Q_p) lifts to K_0^cts(X; Q_p) if and only if the crystalline Chern character ch_crys(x) ∈ ⊕_{i≥0} H^{2i}_crys(X_k; Q_p) maps, under the de Rham-to-crystalline comparison, into ⊕_{i≥0} Fil^{≥i}H^{2i}_dR(X_K/K) ⊆ ⊕_{i≥0} H^{2i}_dR(X_K/K).
items.note: Theorem D of the introduction: the deformation half of the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture, reproved here by the Beilinson fibre square and extended from the smooth proper algebraic case to formal schemes. Nothing in the atlas plans it.

items.name: The fibre square relative to O_K
items.statement: Let X be a smooth formal O_K-scheme. Then there are natural fibre squares with rows K^cts(X; Q_p) → K(X_k; Q_p), TC^cts(X; Q_p) → TC(X_k; Q_p) and HC^{-,cts}(X/O_K; Q_p) → HP^cts(X/O_K; Q_p), stacked so that the outer square is cartesian.
items.note: The geometric, O_K-relative form of the Beilinson square, obtained by Zariski descent from the affine case.

items.name: The p-adic Chern character map for a formal scheme
items.statement: For X/O_K smooth, Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg filtrations together with Adams operations split HP^cts(X/O_K; Q_p) ≃ ∏_{i∈Z} RΓ_dR(X_K/K)[2i] and HC^{-,cts}(X/O_K; Q_p) ≃ ∏_{i∈Z} Fil^{≥i}RΓ_dR(X_K/K)[2i]. Combining with the fibre square gives a natural map K(X_k; Q_p) → TC(X_k; Q_p) → ∏_{i∈Z} RΓ_dR(X_K/K)[2i]. Both source and target depend only on the special fibre, and by left Kan extension from smooth k-algebras the map upgrades to a natural transformation K(Z; Q_p) → TC(Z; Q_p) → ∏_{i∈Z}(RΓ_crys(Z; Q_p) ⊗_{K_0} K)[2i] for every smooth k-scheme Z.
items.note: The construction that produces a crystalline Chern character out of the trace; the reduction to the special fibre alone uses the left Kan extension lemmas of Appendix B.

items.name: The trace-theoretic Chern character is the crystalline one
items.statement: There exists a scalar λ ∈ K^× such that for every smooth separated k-scheme Z the map K_0(Z; Q_p) → ∏_{i≥0} H^{2i}_crys(Z; Q_p) ⊗_{K_0} K constructed above is the crystalline Chern character composed with the automorphism multiplying the i-th factor by λ^i.
items.note: The identification that turns the trace-theoretic statement into the classical one. The λ^i ambiguity is harmless because the conditions in the theorems are stable under it.

items.name: Beilinson's obstruction
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic with perfect residue field k, and let X be a proper O_K-scheme with smooth generic fibre X_K (the special fibre may be singular). Given x ∈ K_i(X_k)_Q there is a natural obstruction class in ⊕_{r≥0} H^{2r−i}_dR(X_K/K)/Fil^r H^{2r−i}_dR(X_K/K) which vanishes if and only if x lifts to (lim_n K_i(X/π^n))_Q. More precisely there is a natural equivalence of spectra cofib(K^cts(X; Q_p) → K(X_k; Q_p)) ≃ ⊕_{r≥0} RΓ_dR(X_K/K)/Fil^{≥r}RΓ_dR(X_K/K)[2r].
items.note: Beilinson's refinement of Bloch–Esnault–Kerz, in the smooth proper case.

items.name: Theorem E: the obstruction for an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme
items.statement: Let X be a qcqs p-adic formal scheme with bounded p-power torsion, and write X_1 = X ×_{Spec Z} F_p. For i ∈ Z and x ∈ K_i(X_1; Q) there is a natural class c(x) ∈ ⊕_{r≥0} H^{2r−i}(LΩ_X/LΩ_X^{≥r})_{Q_p} such that x lifts to K_i^cts(X; Q) if and only if c(x) = 0. More precisely there is a natural equivalence of spectra cofib(K^cts(X; Q) → K(X_1; Q)) ≃ ⊕_{r≥0}(LΩ_X/LΩ_X^{≥r}[2r])_{Q_p}, where LΩ_X is the p-adic derived de Rham cohomology with its derived Hodge filtration.
items.note: The main application of the Beilinson square: Beilinson's obstruction with no smoothness or properness hypothesis, with derived de Rham cohomology in place of de Rham cohomology.

items.name: Theorem G: connectivity of the syntomic complexes
items.statement: (1) If R is a quasisyntomic ring then Z_p(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤i+1}(Z_p), so that Fil^{≥i}TC(R; Z_p) ∈ Sp_{≥i−1}; if R is w-strictly local (for example strictly henselian local) then Z_p(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤i}(Z_p) and Fil^{≥i}TC(R; Z_p) ∈ Sp_{≥i}. (2) The functors R ↦ Z_p(i)(R) and R ↦ Fil^{≥i}TC(R; Z_p) are left Kan extended from finitely generated p-complete polynomial Z_p-algebras.
items.locator: arXiv:2003.12541v2 (29 September 2021), Theorem 5.1; with Theorem G of the introduction
items.note: One of the two structural theorems of Section 5, stated as Theorem G in the introduction. PR.4 plans the syntomic/Tate-twist fibres and their truncation statements and RT.6 the motivic filtration on TC, but this connectivity bound and the left Kan extension property are the paper's own and are not planned.

items.name: Rigidity for the syntomic complexes
items.statement: Let (R, I) be a henselian pair with R and R/I p-complete. Then fib(Z_p(i)(R) → Z_p(i)(R/I)) ∈ D^{≤i}(Z_p).
items.note: The rigidity theorem of Section 5; together with the connectivity bound it is what makes the motivic filtration on TC behave like a motivic filtration. Not planned by any layer.

items.name: p-complete flatness and Tor-amplitude
items.statement: An R-module M is p-completely flat (resp. p-completely faithfully flat) if M ⊗^L_R R/p ∈ D(R/p) is a flat (resp. faithfully flat) R/p-module concentrated in degree zero. An object N ∈ D(R) has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [a,b] if N ⊗^L_R R/p has Tor-amplitude in [a,b].
items.note: DD.0 defines these conditions and proves their compatibility with the alternative formulations of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze §4.

items.name: The quasisyntomic site
items.statement: A commutative ring R is quasisyntomic if it is p-complete, has bounded p-power torsion and L_{R/Z_p} has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1,0]; QSyn is the category of quasisyntomic rings with all ring homomorphisms. Its opposite is a site, with covers the p-completely faithfully flat maps R → R′ of quasisyntomic rings for which L_{R′/R} has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1,0]. A quasisyntomic ring R is quasiregular semiperfectoid if it admits a map from a perfectoid ring and Frobenius on R/p is surjective; these form a basis QRSP ⊆ QSyn of the topology, and a sheaf is determined by its values there by unfolding.
items.note: DD.0 supplies the morphism condition and DD.5 constructs the site together with the existence and refinement of the semiperfectoid covers, which is the unfolding mechanism used throughout Sections 5 and 6.

items.name: Relative quasisyntomic sites
items.statement: For A ∈ QSyn, qSyn^{big}_A is the category of A-algebras B which are quasisyntomic as rings and for which L_{B/A} has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1,0], and qSyn_A ⊆ qSyn^{big}_A is the full subcategory of those B additionally p-completely flat over A; QRSP_A denotes the quasiregular semiperfectoid objects.
items.note: The relative version of the previous item, in the Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze §4.5 range that DD.5 plans; the relative sites over O_K are what Section 5's relative THH argument runs on.

items.name: Prismatic sheaves on the quasisyntomic site
items.statement: For R ∈ QRSP, THH(R; Z_p) is concentrated in even degrees, so the homotopy fixed point and Tate spectral sequences degenerate and TP(R; Z_p) is 2-periodic; one sets Δ_R = π_0(TC^-(R; Z_p)) = π_0(TP(R; Z_p)), the Nygaard ideal N^{≥n}Δ_R = im(π_0((τ_{≥2n}THH(R; Z_p))^{hS^1}) → π_0(THH(R; Z_p)^{hS^1})), and the invertible Breuil–Kisin twists Δ_R{i} = π_{2i}(TP(R; Z_p)) with N^{≥i}Δ_R{i} ≅ π_{2i}(TC^-(R; Z_p)). These extend to D(Z_p)^{≥0}-valued sheaves Δ{i} and N^{≥n}Δ on QSyn by descent.
items.note: RT.6 owns the Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze quasisyntomic THH/TC^-/TP computation and the motivic-filtration interface, including the evenness on quasiregular semiperfectoid covers and the graded comparison with prismatic Δ, Nygaard pieces and Breuil–Kisin twists; PR.3 owns the Nygaard filtration and the twists themselves.

items.name: Perfectoid rings and A_inf
items.statement: Let R_0 be a perfectoid ring. Then Fontaine's ring A_inf(R_0) = W(R_0^♭) carries θ : A_inf(R_0) → R_0, surjective with kernel generated by a non-zero-divisor ξ, and is the universal pro-nilpotent p-complete thickening of R_0. There is a canonical isomorphism Δ_{R_0} ≅ A_inf(R_0) under which a_R is θ, non-canonical isomorphisms Δ_{R_0}{i} ≅ A_inf(R_0), and φ = φ_0 is the Witt vector Frobenius; the Nygaard filtration is the ξ-adic filtration, and φ_i is injective with image (ξ̃^{−min(i,0)}) for ξ̃ = φ(ξ).
items.note: Q0's integral-algebra prefix owns integral perfectoid rings with their A_inf and θ descriptions, and AI.0 the normalisation of ξ, ξ̃ and the Breuil–Kisin twists; RT.6 owns their identification with the THH-theoretic Δ_{R_0}.

items.name: The syntomic complexes Z_p(i)
items.statement: For i ≥ 0 the sheaf Z_p(i) on QSyn is the homotopy equalizer Z_p(i) ≃ fib(N^{≥i}Δ_R{i} →^{can − φ_i} Δ_R{i}). For R ∈ QRSP one has equivalently Z_p(i)(R) = (τ_{[2i−1,2i]}TC(R; Z_p))[−2i]. One also writes F_p(i) = Z_p(i)/p and Q_p(i) = Z_p(i)_{Q_p}.
items.note: PR.4 constructs the syntomic/Tate-twist fibres from the Nygaard pieces and the divided Frobenius with the intrinsic twists, and states that the syntomic realization is shared with RT's TC graded pieces; RT.6 owns that sharing.

planningApi.name: syntomic
planningApi.signature: Define Z_p(i)(R)=fib(can−φ_i:N≥i Δhat_R{i}→Δhat_R{i}) as a sheaf of derived p-complete complexes.

planningApi.name: syntomicGradedTC
planningApi.signature: On the quasiregular semiperfectoid basis identify it with τ[2i−1,2i]TC(R;Z_p)[−2i], then unfold.

planningApi.name: syntomicCoefficients
planningApi.signature: Define F_p(i)=Z_p(i)⊗^L F_p and Q_p(i)=Z_p(i)[1/p]; maps preserve the chosen sign convention.

unitTests.statement: For perfect characteristic-p rings compare with logarithmic de Rham–Witt; retain weight zero separately.
For R=Z_p and i>0, Q_p(i)=Q_p[−1]; shifting by 2i must land in homotopy degree 2i−1.
Check can−φ versus φ−can changes the fibre identification by the prescribed sign.

items.name: The motivic filtrations of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze
items.statement: Let R ∈ QSyn. Then THH(R; Z_p), TC^-(R; Z_p), TP(R; Z_p) and TC(R; Z_p) upgrade to filtered spectra with complete multiplicative descending filtrations, indexed by Z_{≥0}, Z, Z and Z_{≥0}, with graded pieces gr^i THH ≃ N^iΔ_R{i}[2i] (and the twist may be trivialised), gr^i TC^- = N^{≥i}Δ_R{i}[2i], gr^i TP = Δ_R{i}[2i], and gr^i TC = Z_p(i)(R)[2i].
items.note: RT.6 owns exactly this interface: the complete filtrations and their multiplicative, Frobenius-compatible graded comparisons with prismatic Δ, Nygaard pieces, Breuil–Kisin twists and syntomic complexes, with exhaustiveness, completeness and convergence proved rather than assumed.

items.name: Bhatt–Scholze: the syntomic complexes are locally discrete
items.statement: The D(Z_p)^{≥0}-valued sheaf Z_p(i) on QSyn is discrete and torsion free locally: given R ∈ QSyn there is a cover R → R′ in QSyn with Z_p(i)(R′) discrete and torsion free.
items.note: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Theorem 14.1, in the §14 range that PR.4 takes as one of its sources.

items.name: TP modulo ξ̃ and THH^{tC_p}
items.statement: Let R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings) be an algebra over a perfectoid ring R_0. Then TP(R; Z_p)/ξ̃ ≃ THH(R; Z_p)^{tC_p}, and this is concentrated in even degrees and p-torsion free; in particular (p, ξ̃) and (ξ̃, p) are regular sequences on Δ_R.
items.note: The regularity statement that all the modulo-p arguments of Section 5 rest on. RT.6 owns the quasiregular semiperfectoid THH computation but does not plan this consequence.

items.name: The prism structure on Δ_R
items.statement: Let R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings) be an algebra over a perfectoid ring R_0. Then Δ_R = π_0(TP(R; Z_p)) is a prism: φ = φ_0 is congruent to Frobenius modulo p and hence defines a δ-structure by p-torsion-freeness, and I = (ξ̃) ⊆ Δ_R is the kernel of π_0(TP(R; Z_p)) → π_0(THH(R; Z_p)^{tC_p}), independent of R_0. There is a natural map η_R : R → Δ_R/I induced by the cyclotomic Frobenius.
items.note: RT.6 constructs the trace-to-prismatic comparison and PR.0 the prism structure itself; this is the statement that the THH-theoretic Δ_R is a prism in the sense of Bhatt–Scholze.

items.name: Relative topological Hochschild homology over S[z]
items.statement: Let R ∈ qSyn^{big}_{O_K}. Regard R as an S[z]-algebra via z ↦ π for a uniformizer π of O_K and form THH(R/S[z]; Z_p). The construction R ↦ THH(R/S[z]; Z_p) is a sheaf of spectra on qSyn^{big}_{O_K}.
items.note: The device that makes the connectivity bounds provable: relative THH over the cyclotomic base S[z] deforms Hochschild homology relative to O_K. RT.6 owns the absolute BMS2 computation, not this relative one over a polynomial sphere.

items.name: Relative THH of a formally smooth O_K-algebra
items.statement: Let R be a formally smooth O_K-algebra. Then there is a natural isomorphism of graded rings THH_*(R/S[z]; Z_p) ≅ (Ω̂^*_{R/O_K})[u] with |u| = 2.
items.note: The Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg calculation in the relative setting.

items.name: Relative THH of a quasiregular semiperfectoid algebra
items.statement: If R ∈ QRSP_{O_K}, then THH(R/S[z]; Z_p) is concentrated in even degrees and each π_{2n}THH(R/S[z]; Z_p) is a p-completely flat R-module admitting a natural finite increasing filtration with graded pieces the discrete p-completely flat R-modules (∧^j L_{R/O_K})^∧[−j] for j ≤ n.
items.note: Evenness and flatness for the relative theory, the input to the filtration.

items.name: The filtration on relative THH
items.statement: For R ∈ qSyn^{big}_{O_K} there is a multiplicative convergent Z_{≥0}-indexed filtration Fil^{≥⋆}THH(R/S[z]; Z_p) in sheaves of spectra on qSyn^{big}_{O_K}, constructed as in Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze §11 without the flatness hypothesis used there.
items.note: The relative motivic filtration.

items.name: Graded pieces and connectivity of the relative filtration
items.statement: For R ∈ qSyn^{big}_{O_K}, gr^n THH(R/S[z]; Z_p) admits a natural finite increasing filtration with associated graded (∧^j L_{R/O_K})^∧[2n−j] for j ≤ n. In particular gr^n THH(R/S[z]; Z_p) and Fil^{≥n}THH(R/S[z]; Z_p) lie in Sp_{≥n}.
items.note: The connectivity of the relative filtration.

items.name: Relative versus absolute THH
items.statement: If R ∈ QRSP_{O_K}, there are natural surjective maps f_n : π_{2n}THH(R/S[z]; Z_p) → π_{2n−2}THH(R/S[z]; Z_p) and natural isomorphisms π_{2n}THH(R; Z_p) ≅ ker(f_n).
items.note: The comparison that transfers the relative bounds to the absolute theory.

items.name: Connectivity of the filtration on absolute THH
items.statement: If R ∈ qSyn^{big}_{O_K}, then for each n there is a natural fibre sequence gr^n THH(R; Z_p) → gr^n THH(R/S[z]; Z_p) → gr^{n−1}THH(R/S[z]; Z_p)[2]. In particular gr^n THH(R; Z_p) and Fil^{≥n}THH(R; Z_p) lie in Sp_{≥n}.
items.note: The absolute connectivity bound for the THH filtration.

items.name: Connectivity bounds for the Nygaard graded pieces
items.statement: (1) If R ∈ QSyn then N^nΔ_R ∈ D^{≤n}(Z_p). (2) If R → R′ is a surjective map in QSyn then fib(N^nΔ_R → N^nΔ_{R′}) ∈ D^{≤n}(Z_p).
items.note: The first of the connectivity bounds on the prismatic side. PR.3 owns the Nygaard filtration and its graded pieces; these bounds are the paper's own and are what the rigidity theorem is built from.

items.name: Trivialisation of the prism ideal after base change
items.statement: Let R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings) with I ⊆ Δ_R the ideal defining the prism structure. Then there is a natural isomorphism I ⊗_{Δ_R} R ≅ R, i.e. the ideal is naturally trivialized after base change along a_R : Δ_R → R.
items.note: The trivialisation used to define the I-adic twists of the next item.

items.name: Twisting the Nygaard filtration by powers of I
items.statement: For s, i, n ≥ 0 let R ↦ I^s N^{≥n}Δ_R{i} denote the D(Z_p)^{≥0}-valued sheaf on qSyn_{Z_p} obtained by unfolding the discrete sheaf on qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings) given by that formula, where I ⊆ Δ_R is the ideal defining the prism structure; since I is a Cartier divisor, I^s N^{≥n}Δ_R{i} is an invertible twist of N^{≥n}Δ_R{i}.
items.note: The I-adic bookkeeping in which the Frobenius nilpotence argument is carried out.

items.name: Connectivity of the Nygaard quotients
items.statement: Let R ∈ qSyn_{Z_p} and i, n, s ≥ 0. Then the cofibre I^sΔ_R{i}/I^s N^{≥n}Δ_R{i} belongs to D^{≤n−1}(Z_p), and it is left Kan extended from finitely generated p-complete polynomial Z_p-algebras.
items.note: The bound on the Nygaard quotients, with its left Kan extension property.

items.name: A connectivity bound for exterior powers
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M ∈ D^{≤0}(R) with H^0(M) generated by d elements. Then (∧^j M)[−j] ∈ D^{≤d}(R) for all j.
items.note: An elementary derived-algebra lemma. DD.0 constructs the derived exterior powers and their amplitude estimates; this particular bound in terms of the number of generators is not planned.

items.name: Connectivity in terms of the number of generators
items.statement: Let R ∈ qSyn^{big}_{O_K}, let n, i ≥ 0, and suppose H^0(L̂_{R/O_K}) is generated by d elements. Then N^nΔ_R and N^{≥n}Δ_R{i} lie in D^{≤d+1}(Z_p).
items.note: The bound that makes the left Kan extension argument work.

items.name: The Frobenius contracts the Nygaard filtration I-adically
items.statement: Let R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings) and i, r ≥ 0. Then φ_i : N^{≥i}Δ_R{i} → Δ_R{i} carries N^{≥i+r}Δ_R{i} into I^rΔ_R{i}.
items.note: The contraction property at the heart of the Frobenius-nilpotence argument.

items.name: The I-adic filtrations modulo p
items.statement: For R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings) and i, s, r ≥ 0, the map φ_i : N^{≥i+r}Δ_R{i}/p → Δ_R{i}/p is Frobenius semilinear and carries I^s(N^{≥i+r}Δ_R{i}/p) into I^{ps+r}(Δ_R{i}/p); since (p, ξ̃) and (ξ̃, p) are regular sequences on Δ_R, the canonical maps identify these with the corresponding I-adic filtration steps.
items.note: The setting in which the Frobenius becomes topologically nilpotent modulo p.

items.name: The canonical and Frobenius maps are I-adically filtered modulo p
items.statement: Let R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings) and i, r ≥ 0. The maps can and φ_i upgrade to filtered maps for the I-adic filtrations, i.e. there are compatible maps can, φ_i : I^s ⊗_{Δ_R} N^{≥i+r}Δ_R{i}/p → I^s ⊗_{Δ_R} Δ_R{i}/p for each s ≥ 0, and φ_i induces the zero map on associated graded pieces except possibly when s = r = 0.
items.note: The precise nilpotence statement modulo p.

items.name: The Nygaard filtration modulo p is contracted by can − φ_i
items.statement: Let R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings) and i ≥ 0. For r ≫ 0, independent of R, the map can − φ_i : N^{≥i}Δ_R{i}/p → Δ_R{i}/p carries N^{≥i+r}Δ_R{i}/p isomorphically onto itself. Consequently, for such r, F_p(i)(R) ≃ fib(can − φ_i : (N^{≥i}Δ_R{i}/N^{≥i+r}Δ_R{i})/p → (Δ_R{i}/N^{≥i+r}Δ_R{i})/p).
items.note: The finite-level description of F_p(i), from which the left Kan extension property of Theorem G(2) follows.

items.name: A criterion for being left Kan extended
items.statement: Let F, G : QSyn → D(Z_p) be p-complete quasisyntomic sheaves with complete descending Z_{≥0}-indexed filtrations and let F → G be a map of functors, not necessarily filtration preserving. If (1) for R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings) the objects gr^r F(R) and gr^r G(R) are discrete, p-complete and p-torsion free, (2) each gr^r F and gr^r G is left Kan extended from finitely generated p-complete polynomial Z_p-algebras, and (3) there is N such that for r ≥ N and R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings) the map F(R)/p → G(R)/p carries Fil^{≥r}F(R)/p isomorphically onto Fil^{≥r}G(R)/p, then fib(F → G) is p-completely left Kan extended from finitely generated p-complete polynomial Z_p-algebras.
items.note: The general criterion by which Theorem G(2) is proved.

items.name: Left Kan extending the motivic filtration to simplicial commutative rings
items.statement: Since R ↦ Fil^{≥⋆}TC(R; Z_p) is left Kan extended from finitely generated p-complete polynomial algebras, it extends to a functor from p-complete simplicial commutative rings to p-complete filtered spectra commuting with sifted colimits, and one defines Z_p(i)(R) = gr^i TC(R; Z_p)[−2i] on SCR. Moreover, for each i there is r ≫ 0 such that for all p-complete rings R one has F_p(i)(R) ≃ fib(can − φ_i : (N^{≥i}Δ_R{i}/N^{≥i+r}Δ_R{i}) ⊗^L_Z F_p → (Δ_R{i}/N^{≥i+r}Δ_R{i}) ⊗^L_Z F_p).
items.note: The extension of the syntomic complexes beyond quasisyntomic rings; it is what allows Section 4's arguments to be run on simplicial commutative rings and is used again in Section 6.

items.name: A connectivity lemma for filtered objects
items.statement: Let can, φ : Fil^{≥⋆}M → Fil^{≥⋆}N be maps of filtered objects in D(Z) such that (1) both filtrations are complete, (2) φ induces the zero map on associated graded pieces, and (3) there is a fixed r such that for each s the map can : Fil^{≥s}M → Fil^{≥s}N has fibre in D(Z)^{≤r}. Then can − φ : M → N has fibre in D(Z)^{≤r}.
items.note: The formal device converting Frobenius nilpotence into a connectivity bound.

items.name: The connectivity bound over Z_p
items.statement: Let R ∈ qSyn_{Z_p}. Then Z_p(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤i+1}(Z_p) for each i ≥ 0.
items.note: The main case of Theorem G(1).

items.name: Continuity of the syntomic complexes
items.statement: Let R be a noetherian, F-finite, p-complete ring and I ⊆ R an ideal such that R is I-adically complete. Then the natural map Z_p(i)(R) → lim_s Z_p(i)(R/I^s) is an equivalence for every i ≥ 0.
items.note: The continuity statement used to reduce rigidity to a square-zero case.

items.name: Reduction of rigidity to a square-zero case
items.statement: The rigidity theorem holds in general provided it holds for henselian pairs of the form R = A ⊕ N with I = N, where A is the p-completion of a finitely generated Z_p-polynomial algebra, N a finitely generated A-module and R the trivial square-zero extension.
items.note: The reduction step, using continuity and left Kan extension.

items.name: Graded rings and their THH
items.statement: For a commutative monoid M, an M-graded object is a functor from M viewed as a discrete symmetric monoidal category; for an M-graded ring spectrum R_⋆ the twisted Tate diagonal of Appendix A equips THH(R_⋆) with an M-graded cyclotomic structure in which the Frobenius multiplies the grading by p, and the direct sum of the graded pieces recovers THH of the underlying ring as a cyclotomic spectrum.
items.note: The graded framework in which the rigidity theorem is proved; it is supplied by Appendix A and has no counterpart in the atlas.

items.name: Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze for graded rings
items.statement: If the monoid M is uniquely p-divisible, for instance M = Z[1/p]_{≥0}, then the constructions of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze extend to M-graded rings: an M-graded p-complete ring is quasisyntomic (resp. quasiregular semiperfectoid) if its underlying ring is, quasiregular semiperfectoids form a basis of the graded quasisyntomic site (by extracting p-power roots of homogeneous elements, which is where p-divisibility is needed), and one obtains graded objects Δ_{R_⋆}{i} and N^{≥i}Δ_{R_⋆}{i} whose underlying objects need not agree with the ungraded ones.
items.note: The graded version of the whole BMS2 package, built for the proof of rigidity.

items.name: The Frobenius multiplies the grading by p
items.statement: Let R_⋆ be a quasisyntomic Z[1/p]_{≥0}- or Z_{≥0}-graded ring, with underlying p-complete ring R. The finite Nygaard quotient Δ̂_R{i}/N^{≥n}Δ̂_R{i} has the corresponding grading in the p-complete derived category. For r sufficiently large as in (43), the map φ_i : (N^{≥i}Δ̂_R{i}/N^{≥i+r}Δ̂_R{i}) ⊗^L_Z F_p → (Δ̂_R{i}/N^{≥i+r}Δ̂_R{i}) ⊗^L_Z F_p multiplies grading degrees by p.
items.note: The key structural property of the graded theory.

items.name: A graded connectivity lemma
items.statement: Let M, N be Z_{>0}-graded objects of D(F_p) and i ≥ 0. Let can : M → N be a map of graded objects and φ : M → N a map multiplying degrees by p. Suppose (1) the fibre of can belongs to D(F_p)^{≤i} and (2) for any fixed n the cohomologies H^n(M), H^n(N) vanish in all but finitely many degrees of the grading. Then fib(can − φ : M → N) belongs to D(F_p)^{≤i}.
items.note: The graded form of the nilpotence argument, which is what proves rigidity.

items.name: Top cohomology of F_p(i)
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete ring. Then there is a natural isomorphism H^{i+1}(F_p(i)(R)) ≅ coker(1 − C^{−1} : Ω^i_{R/p} → Ω^i_{R/p}/dΩ^{i−1}_{R/p}). In particular, if R is w-strictly local then H^{i+1}(F_p(i)(R)) = H^{i+1}(Z_p(i)(R)) = 0.
items.note: The identification of the top cohomology with an inverse-Cartier cokernel; it is the source of the sharper bound for w-strictly local rings in Theorem G.

items.name: p-adic derived de Rham cohomology
items.statement: For a map of rings A → R, LΩ_{R/A} ∈ D(A) is the p-adic derived de Rham cohomology: the p-completed relative de Rham complex when R is a finitely generated polynomial A-algebra, and in general the p-complete left Kan extension; it agrees with the p-completed underived relative de Rham complex when R is smooth over A. It carries the derived Hodge filtration LΩ^{≥⋆}_{R/A}, obtained by left Kan extending the naive filtration. When A = Z one writes LΩ_R.
items.note: DD.2 constructs derived de Rham cohomology with its Hodge filtration and the comparison with the ordinary complex for smooth maps, and DD.1 the p-completion; this is that object in the p-complete setting.

items.name: Derived de Rham cohomology and divided powers
items.statement: For the map Z[x] → Z one has LΩ_{Z/Z[x]} ≃ Γ̂(x), the p-complete divided power algebra on x, with the Hodge filtration the divided power filtration.
items.note: The basic calculation for a regular quotient; DD.2 names the derived divided-power terms of a singular hypersurface as an acceptance example and DD.3 the regular-quotient/divided-power calculations used in DD.4.

items.name: Derived de Rham–Witt cohomology
items.statement: For an F_p-algebra S, LWΩ_S ∈ D(Z_p) is the p-adic derived de Rham–Witt or derived crystalline cohomology, defined by p-complete left Kan extension from finitely generated polynomial F_p-algebras; for ind-smooth S it agrees with Illusie's WΩ_S. It carries the derived Nygaard filtration N^{≥⋆}LWΩ_S and the divided Frobenius φ_i on N^{≥i}, with p^iφ_i the Frobenius; one writes LWΩ̂_S for the Nygaard completion.
items.note: CR.4 constructs the Witt complexes with Frobenius, Verschiebung and the distinction between the graded and the degree-scaled crystalline Frobenius, and DD.3 the derived Cartier theory from which the derived version is built.

items.name: Sheaf property of derived de Rham–Witt cohomology
items.statement: The functors S ↦ LWΩ_S and S ↦ LWΩ̂_S are sheaves on qSyn_{F_p}.
items.note: The descent statement that lets the equal-characteristic identification be checked on quasiregular semiperfect rings.

items.name: A_crys of a quasiregular semiperfect ring
items.statement: Let S ∈ QRSP_{F_p}. Fontaine's ring A_crys(S) is the universal p-adically complete divided power thickening of S with divided powers compatible with those on (p) ⊆ Z_p; quasiregularity makes it p-torsion free. Then LWΩ_S = A_crys(S), and the Nygaard filtration becomes N^{≥i}A_crys(S) = {x ∈ A_crys(S) : φ(x) ∈ p^iA_crys(S)}, where φ is induced by the Frobenius of S and satisfies φ(x) ≡ x^p mod p, so that A_crys(S) is a δ-ring.
items.note: CR.0 exports the common PD envelope of ker(θ) and its p-completion A_cris by its universal property, so that no second A_cris is built; the identification with derived de Rham–Witt cohomology is the Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze §8.2 statement CR.4 and DD.4 plan.

items.name: The de Rham and de Rham–Witt rings of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring
items.statement: Let R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings). Then LWΩ_{R/p} ≅ A_crys(R/p) is the derived de Rham–Witt cohomology of R/p, and LΩ_R is a discrete, p-complete, p-torsion-free ring with its Hodge filtration; the de Rham-to-crystalline comparison gives a natural map LΩ_R → LWΩ_{R/p} = A_crys(R/p) which is an isomorphism, carrying the Hodge filtration into the Nygaard filtration in the range controlled by the next items.
items.note: The dictionary between the two rings in which the Fontaine–Messing theory and the prismatic theory are written; it is the heart of Section 6.

items.name: Valuation of (pr)! relative to r!
items.statement: For a prime p and r≥0, v_p((pr)!) = v_p(r!) + r; equivalently v_p((pr)!/r!)=r.
items.note: Elementary consequences of Legendre's formula, which Mathlib has as sub_one_mul_padicValNat_factorial ((p−1)·v_p(n!) = n − s_p(n)) together with padicValNat; neither statement is itself a declaration. They are what bound the denominators in the divisibility of the Frobenius below.

items.name: Divisibility of the Frobenius on the Hodge filtration
items.statement: Let R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings). Then for i ≤ p−1 the Frobenius φ : LΩ_R → LΩ_R carries LΩ_R^{≥i} into p^i LΩ_R; equivalently the de Rham-to-crystalline comparison carries LΩ_R^{≥i} into N^{≥i}A_crys(R/p).
items.note: The divisibility that makes the Fontaine–Messing definition of the syntomic complexes possible, and which is exactly why that definition is restricted to weights i ≤ p−2.

items.name: Fontaine–Messing syntomic cohomology
items.statement: Define sheaves on qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings) by Z_p(i)^FM(R) = fib(φ/p^i − 1 : LΩ_R^{≥i} → LΩ_R) for 0 ≤ i ≤ p−2 and Q_p(i)^FM(R) = fib(φ − p^i : LΩ_R^{≥i} → LΩ_R)_{Q_p} for i ≥ 0; these are sheaves because R ↦ LΩ_R^{≥i} is one, and unfolding gives sheaves on qSyn_{Z_p}.
items.note: The classical syntomic complexes of Fontaine and Messing, in derived form. PR.4 constructs the syntomic/Tate-twist fibres from the Nygaard pieces and the divided Frobenius, which is the prismatic description; the de Rham description is a different construction, and the comparison of the two is the main theorem of this section.

items.name: The syntomic complexes in equal characteristic p
items.statement: Let S be a quasisyntomic F_p-algebra. Then for each i: (1) Δ_S{i} is the Nygaard-completed derived de Rham–Witt cohomology LWΩ̂_S, and (2) the Nygaard filtration N^{≥i}Δ_S{i} identifies with the de Rham–Witt Nygaard filtration and φ_i with the divided Frobenius. Consequently Z_p(i)(S) = fib(φ_i − can : N^{≥i}LWΩ̂_S → LWΩ̂_S), and the Nygaard completion is redundant in this formula.
items.note: The Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze §8 identification in equal characteristic, which RT.6 owns as part of the BMS2 interface and PR.4 as the equal-characteristic case of the syntomic fibres.

items.name: The syntomic complexes of a quasiregular semiperfect ring
items.statement: If S is a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra then, for i > 0, Z_p(i)(S) is discrete and p-torsion free, with a natural isomorphism Z_p(i)(S) ≅ (N^{≥i}A_crys(S))^{φ_i = 1}, the fixed points of the divided Frobenius on the i-th Nygaard piece of A_crys(S).
items.note: The concrete description in equal characteristic on the basis of the topology.

items.name: Logarithmic de Rham–Witt forms
items.statement: For an ind-smooth F_p-algebra S, WΩ^•_{S,log} is the graded subring of the de Rham–Witt complex WΩ^•_S of fixed points for F. For S local it is generated modulo any power of p in degree 1 by the elements dlog[x] = d[x]/[x] for x ∈ S^×.
items.note: CR.4 constructs the Witt complexes with Frobenius, Verschiebung, Teichmüller lifts and dlog, which is exactly this subring and its generation.

items.name: The syntomic complexes of an ind-smooth F_p-algebra
items.statement: Let S be an ind-smooth F_p-algebra. Then there are natural identifications Z_p(i)(S) ≃ RΓ_proét(Spec(S), WΩ^i_{−,log})[−i].
items.note: PR.4 plans the logarithmic de Rham–Witt comparisons for the syntomic complexes under the Bhatt–Scholze and Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze hypotheses; this is that comparison in equal characteristic.

items.name: The trace on graded pieces
items.statement: For R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings), HC^-(R; Z_p) is concentrated in even degrees with π_{2i} given by LΩ̂_R^{≥i}; unfolding, the composite K(R; Z_p) → TC(R; Z_p) → HC^-(R; Z_p) induces on graded pieces a natural map Z_p(i)(R) → LΩ̂_R^{≥i} of sheaves on qSyn_{Z_p}; by polynomial left Kan extension it factors naturally through the uncompleted Hodge term LΩ_R^{≥i}.
items.note: The graded form of the left vertical map of the Beilinson square. RT.1 owns HC^- and RT.6 the motivic filtration; the compatibility of the trace with both filtrations is the paper's own.

items.name: The Beilinson fibre square on graded terms
items.statement: Let R ∈ qSyn_{Z_p}. Then for each i ≥ 0 there is a natural map χ_i : Q_p(i)(R/p) → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p} and a functorial pullback square in D(Q_p) with rows Q_p(i)(R) → Q_p(i)(R/p) and (LΩ_R^{≥i})_{Q_p} → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p}. The map χ_i arises from a natural map Z_p(i)(R/p) → p^{−N}LΩ_R for some N ≫ 0 depending only on i, fitting into an analogous diagram. The fibre sequence holds up to isogeny: cofib(Z_p(i)(R) → Z_p(i)(R/p)) and LΩ_R/LΩ_R^{≥i} are naturally isogenous. Finally, for i ≤ p−2 there are natural equivalences fib(Z_p(i)(R) → Z_p(i)(R/p)) ≃ fib(LΩ_R/LΩ_R^{≥i} → LΩ_{R/p}/LΩ_{R/p}^{≥i})[−1].
items.note: RT.3b names this theorem explicitly: it is to export the p-torsion-free p-complete specialization and filtered refinement of AMMN Theorem 6.17 used by PrismaticCohomology PR.7's proof of the prismatic F-crystal/crystalline-lattice equivalence.

items.name: The image of χ_i
items.statement: Let R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} (p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings). Then for each i > 0 the map of Q_p-vector spaces χ_i : Q_p(i)(R/p) → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p} = A_crys(R/p)_{Q_p} is injective with image the φ = p^i eigenspace.
items.note: The identification that turns the graded Beilinson square into the fundamental exact sequence of p-adic Hodge theory in Section 7.

items.name: The Frobenius acts by p^i on the syntomic complexes
items.statement: For any R ∈ qSyn_{F_p}, the Frobenius of R acts as multiplication by p^i on Z_p(i)(R).
items.note: The rigidity that pins down the natural transformation χ_i up to a scalar.

items.name: χ_i is induced from a map in characteristic p
items.statement: For R ∈ qSyn_{Z_p} the natural map χ_i : Z_p(i)(R/p) → p^{−N}LΩ_R → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p} arises, by precomposition with reduction mod p, from a unique natural transformation χ_i : Z_p(i) → p^{−N′}LWΩ_{(−)} on qSyn_{F_p} for some N′ ≥ N.
items.note: The descent of the comparison map to characteristic p, using the Frobenius rigidity.

items.name: Endomorphisms of the graded syntomic ring are scalars
items.statement: Let f : ⊕_{i=0}^N Z_p(i) → ⊕_{i=0}^N Z_p(i) be a natural map of sheaves of graded E_∞-rings on qSyn_{F_p}. Then there is λ ∈ Z_p such that in degree i the map f is multiplication by λ^i.
items.note: The uniqueness statement that identifies the trace-theoretic comparison with the classical one up to a single scalar; the analogue of Proposition 4.12 in the syntomic setting.

items.name: Theorem F: comparison with Fontaine–Messing syntomic cohomology
items.statement: For R ∈ qSyn_{Z_p} there are natural multiplicative identifications Z_p(i)^FM(R) ≃ Z_p(i)(R) for i ≤ p−2, and Q_p(i)^FM(R) ≃ Q_p(i)(R) for all i ≥ 0; that is, Q_p(i)(R) ≃ fib(φ − p^i : LΩ_R^{≥i} → LΩ_R)_{Q_p} and, for i ≤ p−2, Z_p(i)(R) ≃ fib(φ/p^i − id : LΩ_R^{≥i} → LΩ_R).
items.locator: arXiv:2003.12541v2 (29 September 2021), Theorem 6.22; with Theorem F of the introduction
items.note: Theorem F of the introduction: the identification of the graded pieces of the motivic filtration on TC with the syntomic cohomology of Fontaine and Messing. PR.4 constructs the prismatic side and DD.2 the de Rham side, but the comparison is the paper's own and is planned nowhere.

items.name: Corollary H: a de Rham description of rational TC
items.statement: Let R be any simplicial commutative ring. Then there is a natural equivalence TC(R; Q_p) ≃ ⊕_{i≥0} fib(φ − p^i : LΩ_R^{≥i} → LΩ_R)_{Q_p}[2i].
items.locator: arXiv:2003.12541v2 (29 September 2021), Corollary 6.23; with Corollary H of the introduction
items.note: Stated as Corollary H in the introduction: rationally, TC is computed entirely by derived de Rham cohomology with its Hodge filtration and Frobenius.

items.name: Discreteness of the Fontaine–Messing sheaves
items.statement: As D(Z_p)^{≥0}-valued sheaves on qSyn_{Z_p}: (1) Z_p(i)^FM is discrete and torsion free for 0 ≤ i ≤ p−2, and (2) Q_p(i)^FM is discrete.
items.note: The sheaf-theoretic consequence of the comparison, transported from Bhatt–Scholze's theorem.

items.name: Rational K-theory of a p-adic field
items.statement: Let F be a p-adic field, i.e. a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero with perfect residue field of characteristic p. Then, as Q_p-vector spaces, (1) K_{2s}(F; Q_p) = 0 for s > 0, (2) K_{2s−1}(F; Q_p) ≅ F naturally for each s > 1, and (3) there is a natural short exact sequence 0 → F → K_1(F; Q_p) → Q_p → 0.
items.note: KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.6 plans the local-field descriptions, including the rank [L:Q_p] of K_{2j−1}(L; Z_p) for j ≥ 2 and the identification of the torsion by Galois cohomology; this is Wagoner's calculation reproved by the Beilinson square.

items.name: Dimensions and Beilinson–Lichtenbaum
items.statement: If F is a finite extension of Q_p of degree d then dim_{Q_p} K_{2s−1}(F; Q_p) = d+1 for s = 1 and d otherwise. This agrees with Wagoner's calculation of the ranks of the continuous K-groups together with Panin's p-adic continuity, and with the Beilinson–Lichtenbaum prediction K_{2s−1}(F; Q_p) ≅ H^1_ét(F, Q_p(s)), K_{2s−2}(F; Q_p) ≅ H^2_ét(F, Q_p(s)) computed by Tate local duality and the Euler characteristic formula.
items.note: The same statement in numerical form; L.6 plans the ranks and their comparison with the Galois-cohomological description.

items.name: Integral p-adic K-theory of W(k)
items.statement: Assume p > 3. In the range 1 ≤ i ≤ 2p−5 the p-adic K-groups of W(k), for k a perfect field of characteristic p, are K_i(W(k); Z_p) ≅ W(k) for i odd and 0 for i even. The proof runs the integral Beilinson fibre sequence τ_{≤2p−5}ΣHC(W(k), (p); Z_p) → τ_{≤2p−5}K(W(k); Z_p) → Z_p, rewrites the cyclic homology over W(k), uses LΩ_k/LΩ_k^{≥s} ≅ W(k)/p^s for s ≤ p−1 to get π_{2s}HC(k/W(k)) ≅ W(k)/p^{s+1} for i = 2s ≥ 0 and 0 otherwise, and concludes π_{2s}HC(W(k), (p)/W(k)) ≅ p^{s+1}W(k).
items.note: An integral calculation in the range the effective bounds allow, independent of Bökstedt–Madsen and Rognes. KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.5 plans the THH/TR/TC calculations for perfect fields and complete DVRs and L.6 the local higher K-groups; this trace-free derivation from the Beilinson fibre sequence is not planned.

items.name: Integral p-adic K-theory in the ramified case
items.statement: Let F be ramified with O_F/p ≅ k[x]/(x^e), e the absolute ramification degree. Then τ_{≤2p−5}ΣHC(O_F, (p)/W(k)) ≃ τ_{≤2p−5}K(O_F, (p); Z_p), and combining with the known K-theory of truncated polynomial rings over fields — whose positive even p-adic K-groups vanish — gives five-term exact sequences 0 → π_{2s−1}ΣHC(O_F, (p)/W(k)) → K_{2s−1}(O_F; Z_p) → W_{se}(k)/V_eW_s(k) → π_{2s−2}ΣHC(O_F, (p)/W(k)) → K_{2s−2}(O_F; Z_p) → 0 for 2 ≤ s ≤ p−2.
items.note: The ramified companion of the previous item; it gives the low-degree integral p-adic K-groups of O_F independently of Hesselholt–Madsen, or, read the other way, information about the low-degree étale cohomology of F.

items.name: Syntomic cohomology of a discrete valuation ring
items.statement: Let O_F be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0,p) with perfect residue field k. Then (1) Q_p(i)(O_F) ≃ RΓ_proét(Spec(k), Q_p) for i = 0 and F[−1] for i > 0; and (2) in the unramified case O_F = W(k), Z_p(i)(W(k)) ≃ RΓ_proét(Spec(k), Z_p) for i = 0 and W(k)[−1] for 0 < i ≤ p−2.
items.note: The basic computation of the syntomic complexes over a DVR, obtained from the graded Beilinson square. PR.4 plans the syntomic fibres but not this calculation.

items.name: Period rings from the prismatic and de Rham descriptions
items.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring. (1) A_inf(R) with θ : A_inf(R) → R of kernel (ξ) is the prismatic cohomology Δ_R, with the Nygaard filtration the ξ-adic one. (2) A_crys(R) = A_crys(R/p), the p-adic completion of the divided power envelope of (ξ), is identified with the derived de Rham cohomology LΩ_R when R is p-torsion free, with the Hodge filtration the divided power filtration; B_crys^+(R) = A_crys(R)[1/p] carries a Frobenius. (3) B_dR^+(R) = lim_n(A_inf(R)/ξ^n[1/p]) is identified with the Hodge completion of (LΩ_R)_{Q_p} in the p-torsion-free case, with the ξ-adic filtration.
items.note: AI.0 normalises A_inf, θ, ξ and ξ̃ and states that A_cris is the completed PD envelope from CR.0 and B_dR^+ the kernel-adic completion after p-inversion supplied by PadicHodgeTheory; R06.1 constructs B_dR^+, B_dR, B_crys^+ and B_crys from those same objects. What is recorded here is their identification with the prismatic and derived de Rham descriptions.

items.name: The fundamental exact sequence
items.statement: For any perfectoid ring R and i > 0 there is a natural pullback square in D(Q_p) with rows RΓ_proét(Spec(R[1/p]), Q_p(i)) → B_crys^+(R)^{φ = p^i} and Fil^{≥i}B_dR^+(R) → B_dR^+(R). For R = O_C with C complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean this is the usual fundamental exact sequence 0 → Q_p(i) → B_crys^+(O_C)^{φ = p^i} → B_dR^+(O_C)/Fil^{≥i}B_dR^+(O_C) → 0.
items.note: The fundamental exact sequence of p-adic Hodge theory, recovered here from the Beilinson square on graded pieces and the étale comparison. R06.1 constructs B_crys and B_dR^+ with their Frobenius and filtration, but does not plan this exact sequence; it is the classical statement the trace-theoretic square specialises to. This records the paper’s general theorem as a target, not a certified proof: the arbitrary-perfectoid case has the comparison gap E14. The p-torsion-free/O_C application avoids that false integral identification. Route 6 is rejected until this boundary is resolved.

items.name: Identifying the maps of the fundamental exact sequence
items.statement: For C = C_p the map (B_crys^+)^{φ = p} → B_dR^+ produced by the square is Galois-equivariant, and its restriction to Q_p(1) is the dlog map coming from the usual Chern character; since the image of a generator of Q_p(1) is a uniformizer of the DVR B_dR^+, and there is no nonzero Galois-equivariant map C_p → B_dR^+, that restriction determines the map. By Fargues–Fontaine's theorem that ⊕_{i≥0}B_crys^+(O_C)^{φ = p^i} is generated in degree one, the maps for higher i are then determined by multiplicativity.
items.note: The argument that the topologically produced maps are the classical ones; the authors say they know no direct identification. It is exactly the kind of compatibility a formalisation would have to supply.

items.name: p-adic nearby cycles
items.statement: Let X be a formal scheme over O_C and X_proét its pro-étale site. For each i the sheaf of p-adic nearby cycles Rψ_*(Z_p(i)) is the D(Z_p)^{≥0}-valued sheaf on X_proét with RΓ(Spf A, Rψ_*(Z_p(i))) ≃ RΓ_proét(Spec A[1/p], Z_p(i)) for an affine pro-étale open Spf A → X.
items.note: PR.4 plans the nearby-cycle comparisons for the syntomic complexes under the Bhatt–Scholze and Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze hypotheses, of which this is the coefficient object.

items.name: Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze: syntomic complexes as truncated nearby cycles
items.statement: Let R be a formally smooth O_C-algebra and X = Spf(R). Then, as sheaves on X_proét, there is a natural equivalence Z_p(i) ≃ τ^{≤i}Rψ_*(Z_p(i)); in particular Z_p(i)(R) ≃ RΓ(X_proét, τ^{≤i}Rψ_*(Z_p(i))).
items.note: PR.4 plans the stated truncation and nearby-cycle comparisons, warning that syntomic cohomology is not automatically all generic-fibre étale cohomology in every degree; this is that statement.

items.name: De Rham cohomology of formal schemes and rigid spaces
items.statement: For X_0/O_K a smooth proper formal scheme, LΩ_{X_0/O_K} is the p-adic derived de Rham cohomology with its Hodge filtration; it is also the p-complete usual de Rham complex, the Hodge filtration is finite, LΩ_{X_0/O_K} is a perfect O_K-module, and its rationalization Ω_{X_0/K} is the de Rham cohomology of the rigid generic fibre, a perfect K-module.
items.note: DD.2 constructs derived de Rham cohomology with its Hodge filtration and its comparison with the ordinary complex for smooth maps; DD.1 supplies the p-completion.

items.name: The Colmez–Nizioł and Tsuji comparison
items.statement: Let X_0/O_K be a smooth proper formal scheme, X its base change to O_C, and X̄_0 its reduction modulo π. For each i ≥ 0 there is a natural pullback square in D(Q_p) with rows RΓ(X_proét, τ^{≤i}Rψ_*(Q_p(i))) → (A_crys ⊗_{W(k)} RΓ_crys(X̄_0/W(k)))^{φ = p^i}[1/p] and Fil^{≥i}(Ω_{X_0/K} ⊗_K B_dR^+) → (Ω_{X_0/K} ⊗_K B_dR^+).
items.note: The semistable-free case of the Colmez–Nizioł and Tsuji comparison between p-adic nearby cycles and syntomic cohomology, recovered here from the graded Beilinson square. CohomologyComparisons CP.2 owns the rational crystalline comparison and CP.3 the B_dR^+ deformation; this square, which is their common refinement in the truncated nearby-cycle form, is not planned.

items.name: L-twisted diagonals and Tate diagonals
items.statement: Let C be a presentably symmetric monoidal ∞-category and L : C → C a left adjoint symmetric monoidal functor. An L-twisted diagonal on C is a symmetric monoidal natural transformation Δ : L(C) → (C ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ C)^{hC_p} of lax symmetric monoidal functors. If C is stable (or merely semiadditive), an L-twisted Tate diagonal is a symmetric monoidal natural transformation Δ : L(C) → T_p(C) := (C ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ C)^{tC_p}.
items.note: The generalisation of the Tate diagonal of Nikolaus–Scholze which produces cyclotomic structures on Hochschild homology in categories other than spectra. RT.2 constructs the cyclotomic Frobenius in spectra; nothing plans the twisted version, which is what gives THH of a graded or filtered ring its graded or filtered cyclotomic structure.

planningApi.name: twistedDiagonal
planningApi.signature: For presentably symmetric monoidal C, a symmetric monoidal left adjoint L:C→C, and prime p, specify a monoidal natural transformation L(X)→(X^⊗p)^hCp.

planningApi.name: twistedTateDiagonal
planningApi.signature: In the source’s stable/semiadditive setting replace homotopy fixed points by the Tate construction; retain compatibility with the lax monoidal structures.

planningApi.name: gradedExample
planningApi.signature: For additive grading, the p-fold tensor sends degree d to pd; the total-object functor is a direct sum, and degree-zero evaluation is a different functor.

unitTests.statement: The unit lies in grading zero.
At p=3,d=2 the output degree is 6, not 8.
An unstable diagonal on Fun(I,Spaces) must not be silently typed as the Cartesian structure on Fun(I,Spectra).

items.name: Cyclotomic bases
items.statement: If R is an E_∞-ring and C = Mod_R, every left adjoint symmetric monoidal L is induction along an E_∞-map l : R → R, and the datum of an L-twisted Tate diagonal on C is equivalent to an E_∞-homotopy between R →^{l} R →^{triv} R^{tC_p} and the Tate-valued Frobenius φ : R → R^{tC_p}. An E_∞-ring with such a datum is a cyclotomic base; S[z] is one.
items.note: The notion that makes THH(−/S[z]) of Section 5 a cyclotomic object, which is what the relative filtration argument needs.

items.name: Twisted cyclotomic structures on Hochschild homology
items.statement: If C is equipped with an L-twisted diagonal (resp. Tate diagonal), then every algebra object A ∈ Alg(C) acquires an induced S^1-equivariant map L(HH A) → (HH A)^{hC_p} (resp. L(HH A) → (HH A)^{tC_p}), functorially and symmetric monoidally in A.
items.note: The mechanism producing the twisted cyclotomic structure.

items.name: Stabilisation of a twisted diagonal
items.statement: For a given L-twisted diagonal on C, the stabilization Sp(C) admits a canonical induced Sp(L)-twisted Tate diagonal.
items.note: Passage from spaces to spectra.

items.name: A criterion on the indexing category
items.statement: Let I be a symmetric monoidal ∞-category such that for all objects i, j ∈ I the forgetful map Map_I(i^{⊗p}, j)^{hC_p} → Map_I(i^{⊗p}, j) is an equivalence; equivalently, (i^{⊗p})_{hC_p} exists in I and i^{⊗p} → (i^{⊗p})_{hC_p} is an equivalence. Then Fun(I, S) admits an L_p-twisted diagonal, where L_p is left Kan extension along l_p : I → I, i ↦ i^{⊗p}.
items.note: The combinatorial criterion by which the graded, filtered and S[z]-linear cases are all handled at once.

items.name: Twisted cyclotomic structure on functor categories
items.statement: If I satisfies the criterion above, then for every algebra A in Fun(I, Sp) there is a twisted cyclotomic structure on HH A, i.e. a natural symmetric monoidal S^1-equivariant map L_p(HH A) → (HH A)^{tC_p}.
items.note: The output of the criterion.

items.name: The graded, filtered and polynomial instances
items.statement: The categories I = Z_{≥0}^{ds} (graded spectra), I = Z_{≥0}^{op} (filtered spectra) and I = BZ_{≥0} (so that Fun(I, Sp) ≃ Mod_{S[z]}) all satisfy the criterion, so graded, filtered and S[z]-linear ring spectra have THH with a twisted cyclotomic structure in which the Frobenius multiplies the grading, resp. the filtration index, by p.
items.locator: arXiv:2003.12541v2 (29 September 2021), Example A.10; Examples A.10–A.12
items.note: The three instances the paper uses: the graded one for the rigidity proof of Section 5, the S[z]-linear one for the relative THH of Section 5.

items.name: Symmetric monoidal categories with (Tate) diagonals and their maps
items.statement: A symmetric monoidal category with (Tate) diagonals is a triple (C, L, Δ). A map (C, L, Δ) → (C′, L′, Δ′) is a left adjoint symmetric monoidal functor F : C → C′ together with a symmetric monoidal equivalence L′ ∘ F ≃ F ∘ L and a natural symmetric monoidal equivalence between the induced diagonals.
items.note: The functoriality needed to compare the graded and ungraded theories.

items.name: Left Kan extension preserves twisted diagonals
items.statement: If f : I → I′ is a symmetric monoidal functor between categories satisfying the criterion, then left Kan extension along f induces a map of symmetric monoidal ∞-categories with diagonals (Fun(I, S), L_p, Δ) → (Fun(I′, S), L′_p, Δ′). Consequently, for every algebra A ∈ Fun(I, Sp) there is an equivalence F(HH A) ≃ HH(FA) of L′_p-twisted cyclotomic objects, where F is left Kan extension along f.
items.locator: arXiv:2003.12541v2 (29 September 2021), Lemma A.14; with Corollary A.15
items.note: The compatibility that identifies the total THH of a graded ring with THH of its underlying ring.

items.name: Total THH of a graded or filtered ring spectrum
items.statement: For a nonnegatively graded ring spectrum R_•, ⊕_i THH(R_•)_i ≃ THH(⊕_i R_i) as cyclotomic spectra. For a filtered ring spectrum, the underlying filtered-colimit functor preserves the twisted structure and recovers THH of the underlying ring. Separately, for nonnegatively graded ring spectra, THH(R_•)_0 ≃ THH(R_0) as cyclotomic spectra.
items.locator: arXiv:2003.12541v2 (29 September 2021), Example A.16; with Example A.17
items.note: The concrete consequence used in Sections 3 and 5.

items.name: Left Kan extension from polynomial algebras
items.statement: Let R be a ring and Poly_R the category of finitely generated polynomial R-algebras. Given a presentable ∞-category C and an accessible functor f : Poly_R → C, left Kan extension gives Lf : SCR_R → C commuting with geometric realizations, where SCR_R is the ∞-category of simplicial commutative R-algebras.
items.note: E5:animation constructs animated commutative algebras from simplicial commutative rings, polynomial resolutions and sifted left Kan extensions, and E3 proves the left Kan extension theorem with its pointwise formula and uniqueness.

items.name: A Frobenius factorisation for simplicial commutative F_p-algebras
items.statement: Let R ∈ SCR_{F_p}. There is a natural map f : R → R ⊗^L_Z F_p in SCR_{F_p} such that the composites R →^{f} R ⊗^L_Z F_p → R and R ⊗^L_Z F_p → R → R ⊗^L_Z F_p are the respective Frobenius endomorphisms.
items.note: The factorisation that lets a natural transformation defined after base change along Z → F_p be descended, at the cost of a power of p. Nothing in the atlas plans the Frobenius on animated F_p-algebras in this form.

items.name: Descending a natural transformation along reduction mod p
items.statement: Let F_1, F_2 : SCR_{F_p} → D(Z) be functors and suppose the Frobenius acts on F_1(R) as multiplication by p^i. Then for any natural transformation u : F_1(− ⊗^L_Z F_p) → F_2(− ⊗^L_Z F_p) of functors SCR_Z → D(Z), the transformation p^i u arises from a natural transformation F_1 → F_2.
