items.note: The formal engine behind Corollary 6.20: the comparison map χ_i is defined only after reduction mod p, and this is how it is descended with a controlled denominator.

items.name: Almost finitely presented animated algebras
items.statement: SCR^{afp}_k is the ∞-category of simplicial commutative k-algebras R that are almost finitely presented, i.e. π_0(R) is a finitely generated k-algebra and each π_i(R) is a finitely generated π_0(R)-module; equivalently R is a geometric realization of a simplicial diagram of finitely generated polynomial k-algebras. Similarly SCR̂^{afp}_{O_K} consists of π-complete simplicial commutative O_K-algebras with π_0 topologically finitely generated and each π_i finitely generated.
items.note: The finiteness conditions under which the special-fibre comparison of Section 4 is proved. E5:animation constructs animated algebras but does not plan these finiteness classes.

items.name: Comparing natural transformations on smooth algebras and formal schemes
items.statement: Let E be an ∞-category admitting sifted colimits and F_1, F_2 : SCR^{afp}_k → E functors such that (1) F_1 commutes with geometric realizations and (2) F_1(R) ≃ F_1(π_0 R) for R ∈ SCR^{afp}_k. Then Hom_{Fun(Sm_k, E)}(F_1, F_2) ≃ Hom_{Fun(FSm_{O_K}, E)}(F_1(− ⊗_{O_K} k), F_2(− ⊗_{O_K} k)), so that a natural transformation of functors of formally smooth O_K-algebras that depends only on the special fibre descends to one of functors of smooth k-algebras.
items.note: The lemma that lets the p-adic Chern character of Section 4, defined on formal schemes over O_K, be recognised as a transformation depending only on the special fibre — the step that identifies it with the crystalline Chern character.

items.name: Valuation bound for p^r/r!
items.statement: For a prime p and r≥0, v_p(p^r/r!)≥min(r,p−1).
items.note: Derive from pinned Legendre bounds; the exact min(r,p−1) bound was not found. Keep the source proof step separate from the existing factorial identity.
proofSteps: For 0≤r<p, r! is prime to p. For r≥p, Legendre gives r−v_p(r!)=(r(p−2)+s_p(r))/(p−1). For p=2 the nonzero digit sum is at least 1. For p>2 use r≥p and s_p(r)≥1 to obtain at least p−1. Do not assume r−v_p(r!) is monotone.

items.name: The henselian K-theory Beilinson square
items.statement: For an associative ring R there is a natural tr_crys : K(R/p;Q_p)→HP(R;Q_p) and a commutative square with top K(R;Q_p)→K(R/p;Q_p), bottom HC^−(R;Q_p)→HP(R;Q_p), left tr_GJ, right tr_crys. If R is commutative and henselian along (p), the square is cartesian and K(R,(p);Q_p)≃ΣHC(R;Q_p). Q_p means p-completion followed by inversion of p.
items.locator: AMMN Theorem A p.3 and proof p.11
items.note: The original extraction had the TC square and a fibre conclusion, but no exact map-level K square.

items.name: Connectivity of TC
items.statement: If a bounded-below cyclotomic spectrum X has n-connective underlying spectrum, TC(X;Z_p) is (n−1)-connective.
items.note: Used repeatedly to commute realizations and control the comparison ranges.

items.name: Closure properties of quasi-isogenies
items.statement: In a stable ∞-category with left-complete t-structure, a map of bounded-below objects is a quasi-isogeny exactly when its fibre is quasi-isogenous to zero. On connective objects quasi-isogenies are stable under finite colimits and geometric realizations; right-bounded exact functors preserve them. A natural quasi-isogeny is defined in the pointwise functor category and requires degreewise denominator bounds uniform in the indexing object.
items.note: Preserve the uniformity used in the proof of Theorem 3.4; arbitrary filtered colimits are excluded.

items.name: Formality up to quasi-isogeny
items.statement: Every bounded-below spectrum X is related by a zig-zag of quasi-isogenies to ⊕_n Hπ_n(X)[n]. This is not a canonical functorial splitting; uniform bounds for the k-invariants are the input.
items.locator: AMMN Example 2.19 p.12; Beilinson14 and Mathew16
items.note: Record the explicit source boundary for the noncanonical formality example.

items.name: Relative THH base-change comparisons
items.statement: Let O_K be a complete mixed-characteristic DVR with perfect residue field k and uniformizer π, and R∈QSyn_{O_K}. For S[z]→R, z↦π, there are natural equivalences THH(R/S[z];Z_p)⊗^L_{O_K}k≃THH(R⊗^L_{O_K}k;Z_p) and THH(R/S[z];Z_p)⊗^L_{THH(O_K/S[z];Z_p)}O_K≃HH(R/O_K;Z_p).
items.note: The original item61 omitted the two comparisons used to prove its successors.

items.name: Left Kan extension of THH filtration pieces
items.statement: The relative gr^n and Fil^{≥n} THH over S[z], on QSyn_{O_K}, are p-completely left Kan extended from finite p-complete polynomial O_K-algebras. The absolute gr^n and Fil^{≥n} THH on QSyn are p-completely left Kan extended from finite p-complete polynomial Z_p-algebras.
items.note: These clauses are omitted from items65/67 but used in Theorem5.1.

items.name: Finite-coefficient pro-continuity of syntomic complexes
items.statement: For a p-complete ring R with bounded p-power torsion and fixed r≥1, Z_p(i)(R)/p^r→{Z_p(i)(R/p^s)/p^r}_s induces isomorphisms of pro cohomology groups.
items.note: Uses pro Tor-unitality of (p), the finite Nygaard quotient formula and continuity of derived exterior powers.

items.name: Syntomic rigidity for a finite square-zero extension
items.statement: If A is a finite p-complete polynomial Z_p-algebra and N a finite A-module, for R=A⊕N the fibre Z_p(i)(R)→Z_p(i)(A) lies in D^{≤i}(Z_p).
items.note: Item83 stated only a reduction conditional on this theorem; the actual base case must be a target.

items.name: The truncated universal divided-power calculation
items.statement: For perfect k of characteristic p and 1≤r≤p, the Hodge quotient of p-completed derived de Rham LΩ_{k/W(k)}/F^r is W(k)/p^r, including r=p. It is the cokernel of x−p on the free truncated PD module with basis γ_0(x),…,γ_{r−1}(x).
items.locator: AMMN Example7.3 p.50; SZ18 Proposition3.16 pp.32–36; Bhatt12 Proposition8.5 p.32
items.note: Independent calculation rejects E1. No cancellation of p! is allowed in the universal PD algebra.

items.name: Descent of natural transformations through an adjunction
items.statement: For an adjunction L:C⇄D:R and functors f1,f2:D→E, if f1(LRx)→f1(x) is an equivalence for every x, then Map_{Fun(D,E)}(f1,f2)≃Map_{Fun(C,E)}(f1∘L,f2∘L).
items.note: The explicit adjunction lemma supplies CorollaryB.6, independently of its arithmetic specialization.

items.name: The existing Fontaine theta map
items.statement: For a commutative p-adically complete ring R and prime p with p nonunit, the pinned map θ:W(PreTilt(R,p))→R evaluates Teichmüller representatives by untilt; it is surjective when Frobenius on R/p is surjective.
items.note: Import the existing map; the perfectoid principal-kernel theorem and prismatic comparison remain separate planned mathematics.

items.name: The existing de Rham period-ring carrier
items.statement: For a commutative p-adically complete R with p prime and nonunit, BDeRhamPlus R p is the ordinary completion of W(PreTilt(R,p))[1/p] at the kernel of θ[1/p].
items.note: Reuse the existing carrier. Kernel principality, comparison to the displayed ξ-adic presentation, DVR structure, period invariants and derived de Rham comparison are not provided by this definition.

prerequisites.citation: Spencer Bloch, Hélène Esnault and Moritz Kerz, p-adic deformation of algebraic cycle classes, Invent. Math. 195 (2014), 673–722
prerequisites.why: The theorem reproved and extended in Section 4: a class in K_0 of the special fibre of a proper smooth p-adic formal scheme lifts to continuous K-theory exactly when its crystalline Chern character lies in the Hodge filtration. Nothing in the atlas plans it or the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture it is aimed at.

prerequisites.citation: Thomas Geisser and Lars Hesselholt, On relative and bi-relative algebraic K-theory of rings of finite characteristic, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 24 (2011), 29–49
prerequisites.why: The theorem that relative K-theory of a nilpotent ideal in a ring in which p is nilpotent is torsion, recovered here as a corollary of Theorem C and used for the continuity of continuous K-theory.

routes.title: Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods, Part II: p-adic deformation of K-theory classes
routes.brief: Plan the p-adic deformation of K-theory classes: continuous K-theory of p-adic formal schemes, the obstruction to deforming a class from the special fibre, and the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture of Fontaine and Messing that the obstruction theory is aimed at. The final theorems are Theorem D and Theorem E of Antieau, Mathew, Morrow and Nikolaus. Theorem D (their Theorem 4.9, the theorem of Bloch, Esnault and Kerz): for K a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero with ring of integers O_K and perfect residue field k of characteristic p, and X → Spf(O_K) a proper smooth p-adic formal scheme, a class x ∈ K_0(X_k; Q_p) lifts to K_0^cts(X; Q_p) if and only if its crystalline Chern character ch_crys(x) ∈ ⊕_i H^{2i}_crys(X_k; Q_p) is carried by the de Rham-to-crystalline comparison into ⊕_i Fil^{≥i}H^{2i}_dR(X_K/K). Theorem E (their Theorem 4.14): for X a qcqs p-adic formal scheme with bounded p-power torsion and x ∈ K_i(X_1; Q), there is a natural class c(x) ∈ ⊕_{r≥0}H^{2r−i}(LΩ_X/LΩ_X^{≥r})_{Q_p} vanishing exactly when x lifts to K_i^cts(X; Q), and more precisely a natural equivalence cofib(K^cts(X; Q) → K(X_1; Q)) ≃ ⊕_{r≥0}(LΩ_X/LΩ_X^{≥r}[2r])_{Q_p} in terms of p-adic derived de Rham cohomology with its derived Hodge filtration. The roadmap must cover: continuous invariants F^cts(X) = lim_n F(X_n) of a p-adic formal scheme for F = K, THH, HH, HC^-, HP, TC, with the continuity theorems saying which comparison maps F(X) → F^cts(X) are p-adic equivalences and the warning that for K and a proper scheme this is expected to fail; the crystalline Chern character of a regular scheme of characteristic p, with its Chern classes and the usual axioms; the de Rham cohomology of a smooth p-adic formal scheme with its Hodge filtration, and Berthelot–Ogus's rationalised comparison with the crystalline cohomology of the special fibre; the stacked fibre squares relating K^cts, TC^cts, HC^{-,cts} and HP^cts of a smooth formal O_K-scheme; the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg splitting of HP^cts and HC^{-,cts} into de Rham cohomology and its Hodge filtration, and the resulting p-adic Chern character map, together with the proof that it depends only on the special fibre and is the crystalline Chern character up to a scalar λ^i; Beilinson's obstruction in the proper smooth case and its generalisation, Theorem E; and the statement of the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture itself, recorded as a conjecture with its exact hypotheses and not as a theorem. Import, and do not re-plan: the Beilinson fibre square, the quasi-isogeny comparison of cyclotomic spectra and the p-adic Chern character tr_crys from Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods (RefinedTraceMethods), stage RT.3b, of which this paper is also the source; the cyclotomic trace, the Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy theorem and the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow comparison K(R,(p);Z_p) ≃ TC(R,(p);Z_p) for a ring henselian along (p) from RT.3; Hochschild, cyclic, negative cyclic and periodic cyclic homology with the SBI sequence from RT.1; THH, TC^-, TP and TC from RT.2; and the motivic filtration on TC with its graded pieces from RT.6. Import relative and nonconnective K-theory from General algebraic K-theory (GeneralAlgebraicKTheory), stages K.5 and K.6, and Chern classes, the Chern character and the γ-filtration from K-theory of schemes, localisation and operations (SchemeKTheoryOperations), stage S.7. Import the cotangent complex and its derived exterior powers from Derived de Rham cohomology and its algebraic foundations (DerivedDeRhamCohomology), stage DD.0, derived completion from DD.1, derived de Rham cohomology with its Hodge filtration from DD.2, and the crystalline comparison from DD.4. Import crystalline cohomology, its sites and crystals from Crystalline cohomology, de Rham–Witt and logarithmic foundations (CrystallineCohomology), stages CR.0 and CR.1, and the rational crystalline comparison for a smooth proper formal O_K-model from Cohomology comparisons (CohomologyComparisons), stage CP.2. Record with the statement of the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture that it is open, and that Motives and algebraic cycles (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles) stage MC.7 owns the register of cycle conjectures and their proved cases, so that the conjecture is cross-referenced there rather than restated. The roadmap owns, and must plan itself, continuous K-theory and the other continuous invariants of a formal scheme, the crystalline Chern character, the identification of the trace-theoretic Chern character with it, and the two obstruction theorems. INDEPENDENT REVIEW CORRECTIONS: import formal de Rham cohomology and proper-smooth Hodge degeneration from DD.2/DD.5 and CP.3; import the conjectural proposition from MC.7. Construct only the crystalline specialization/compatibility of the degree-zero Chern character, importing the generic S.7 construction. Its value on a line bundle is exp(c1), not 1+c1. This route is not ready for a design job: resolve the recorded source/API/dependency gaps first.
routes.reason: Section 4 of the paper is a self-contained body of mathematics that the atlas heads towards nowhere: continuous K-theory K^cts(X) = lim_n K(X_n) of a p-adic formal scheme and the other continuous trace invariants, the crystalline Chern character, the identification of the trace-theoretic Chern character with it, Beilinson's obstruction class, its generalisation to arbitrary qcqs formal schemes with derived de Rham cohomology in place of de Rham cohomology, the Bloch–Esnault–Kerz theorem, and the statement of the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture. A search of the layer descriptions finds no 'continuous K-theory', no 'Bloch–Esnault–Kerz' and no 'variational Hodge'; MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.7 plans a register of cycle conjectures but names only the Hodge, Tate and standard conjectures and the Bloch–Beilinson filtration, and it plans none of the K-theoretic machinery in which the p-adic conjecture is posed. These are new layers in the direction RefinedTraceMethods already goes: they are the application for which the Beilinson fibre square of RT.3b was proved, they use RT.1's cyclic homology, RT.2's THH and TC, RT.3's cyclotomic trace and Clausen–Mathew–Morrow comparison and RT.3b's square as their entire machinery, and RT's own summary calls it a shared trace-theoretic library whose arithmetic applications live in its consumers. So this is a Part II of RefinedTraceMethods rather than a new roadmap. The alternative parent is MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles, whose MC.7 would then acquire the p-adic variational Hodge conjecture and its deformation theory; a reviewer who prefers that should say so, and the brief transfers with the imports reversed. The case for RefinedTraceMethods is that everything here is proved by trace methods and that the only statement about cycles is the conjecture itself, which the brief instructs the design job to cross-reference to MC.7 rather than restate. Independent review finds the deformation direction appropriate, but generic de Rham and conjecture-register work have existing owners. The route is rejected pending the explicit closure gaps.

RT.3b already exists for this paper: it is titled 'The Beilinson square and the prismatic F-crystal proof bridge' and instructs the blueprint to prove Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus Theorem 2.12 and Corollary 3.9, to supply the quasi-isogeny comparison of their Section 3, to prove the shift dictionary fib(TC(R;Q_p)→TC(R/p;Q_p)) ≃ ΣHC(R;Q_p), and to export the filtered refinement of their Theorem 6.17 that PrismaticCohomology PR.7 uses. Those four statements are therefore planned; what is not planned, and what this route supplies, is everything the proof needs. From Section 2: the cyclotomic spectrum Z_{hC_p} and the cofibre sequence Z_{hC_p} → Z^triv → THH(F_p), the Tate vanishing lemma, the cartesian square of cyclotomic spectra and its TC^-/TP form, the effective bounds on the denominators that give every range of the form 2p − c in the paper, the notion of isogeny and quasi-isogeny, the integral statements Theorem A and Corollary B with their truncation ranges, and the relative statement for a nilpotent ideal. From Section 3, the whole theory of quasi-isogenies of cyclotomic spectra: the TR criterion, the two vanishing criteria, Theorem C on THH of a quasi-isogeny with nilpotent kernel on π_0, its graded, square-zero and augmented cases, and the recovery of Geisser–Hesselholt's theorem. From Section 5, the relative THH over the cyclotomic base S[z] with its filtration and connectivity bounds, and the graded version of the Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze package, which RT.6 owns in its ungraded form. From Section 6, the compatibility of the trace with both filtrations on graded pieces. From Appendix A, the twisted Tate diagonals: the general notion, cyclotomic bases, the criterion on an indexing category, and the graded, filtered and S[z]-linear instances, which is how a graded ring gets a graded cyclotomic structure on its THH — RT.2 constructs the cyclotomic Frobenius in spectra and nothing plans this. The route also names the four planned statements above and the two Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze statements of Section 5 that RT.6 owns, because this paper is their designated source.

PR.4 owns the syntomic complexes: it constructs the syntomic and Tate-twist fibres from the Nygaard pieces and the divided Frobenius with the intrinsic twists, proves the truncation and nearby-cycle and logarithmic de Rham–Witt comparisons, and states that its syntomic realization is shared with RT's TC graded pieces; PR.3 owns the Nygaard filtration, the divided Frobenius and the Breuil–Kisin twists. Sections 5 and 6 of this paper prove what those layers need and do not plan. The structural theorems are the connectivity bound Z_p(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤i+1}(Z_p), sharpened to D^{≤i} for w-strictly local rings, with its consequence that Fil^{≥i}TC(R;Z_p) is (i−1)-connective; the left Kan extension of Z_p(i) and of the motivic filtration from finitely generated p-complete polynomial algebras, hence their definition on all simplicial commutative rings; and the rigidity theorem, that fib(Z_p(i)(R) → Z_p(i)(R/I)) ∈ D^{≤i}(Z_p) for a henselian pair of p-complete rings. The route also carries their whole proof: the connectivity bounds on the Nygaard graded pieces and quotients, the I-adic filtrations modulo p and the nilpotence of the Frobenius on them, the finite-level description of F_p(i), the criteria for being left Kan extended, the continuity statement, and the graded connectivity lemma. Section 6 then supplies the comparison the layer most needs: the Fontaine–Messing description Z_p(i)(R) ≃ fib(φ/p^i − id : LΩ_R^{≥i} → LΩ_R) for i ≤ p−2 and its rational form for all i, with the divisibility of the Frobenius on the Hodge filtration that makes the definition possible, the identification of the image of χ_i with a Frobenius eigenspace, the rigidity of the Frobenius action that pins the comparison down up to a scalar, and the resulting de Rham description of TC(R; Q_p). The computation of the syntomic complexes of a complete discrete valuation ring belongs with them. Generic Lemma5.26 and filtered connectivity lemmas5.34/5.42 now import DD.0/DD.1; Proposition5.32 imports EDS E3. The rational TC decomposition, with [2i], is owned by RT.6.

E5:animation constructs animated commutative algebras from simplicial commutative rings, polynomial resolutions and sifted left Kan extensions, and E3 proves the left Kan extension theorem with its pointwise formula, uniqueness and cofinality.
